subject: 📢  UXfolio Product Brief: Sharper case studies. Stronger first impressions.  Here’s what’s new. 🔥
body_text:
Hey Jasmin Duong,

February brought a mix of new features and thoughtful refinements
to UXfolio.

We were focusing on deliberate improvements that make your
portfolio clearer, more structured, and more intentional.

Over the past month, we targeted two areas:

* strengthening how your work appears at first glance
* improving how you build and iterate behind the scenes

*************************
This month’s highlights:
*************************

-------------------------
🖼️ Thumbnail backgrounds
-------------------------

Elevate your case study thumbnails with custom images and
abstract backgrounds.

Image

In a portfolio grid, thumbnails determine which project gets
attention first. With custom images and abstract backgrounds, you
can create stronger visual contrast so your case studies stand
out and attract more clicks.

How to use it
-------------

* Click Set thumbnail on your case study.
* In the pop-up window, select the Background tab.
* Choose a background type and color, or upload your own image.

Take a minute to experiment with your thumbnails and see how
easily you can elevate the look of your portfolio.

---------------
🧩 Cards section
---------------

Highlight the key insights and impact in your case studies using
the Cards section.

Image

The Cards section helps you pull key insights out of long case
study narratives and present them in a clear, high-visibility
format. Instead of hiding impact inside paragraphs, you can
highlight metrics, decisions, and learnings so readers
immediately see the value of your work.

How to use it
-------------

* Click Add section in your case study.
* Select the Cards section that fits your content best.
* Customize the cards with your key insights, metrics, or
decisions to highlight the most important takeaways.

Try adding a few Cards to your next case study and see how
quickly your key insights become easier to spot.

-----------------
🔵 Corner rounding
-----------------

Make your portfolio consistent by setting balanced corners for
all images.

Image

Consistent corner rounding helps your portfolio feel more
polished and intentional. With shared corner radius settings
across elements like thumbnails, images, case study cards, and
other sections, you can maintain one cohesive visual style and
eliminate small inconsistencies that quietly affect perception.

How to use it
-------------

* Select the object you want to edit (image, thumbnail, or card)
and click Edit corner radius.
* Adjust the radius to the value that fits your preferred visual
style.
* Apply the setting to create a consistent, balanced look across
your portfolio.

Take a minute to refine your corner radius and see how quickly
your portfolio starts to feel more cohesive and professional.

***********************************
⚙️ Additional features of the month
***********************************

New Add Section modal with previews: The new Add Section modal
now includes previews, so you can choose the right structural
block faster and with more confidence.

Refactored mockup UX for media modules: Media modules now have a
refactored mockup editing flow, giving you clearer control and
faster adjustments when presenting visuals.

Hidden case study preview: You can prepare case studies privately
using hidden previews before publishing them. Work in progress
stays private until you decide it’s ready.

Section duplication: You can duplicate sections in one click,
making iteration easier when you want to test variations or
repeat a strong structural pattern.

Related case studies: Now with Related case studies, you can
guide readers from one project to another, building narrative
continuity instead of isolated examples.

Individually, these are small improvements. Together, they reduce
friction. And when friction drops, quality rises.

-----------------------------
📌 Why does this month matter?
-----------------------------

February’s updates give you more control over how your work
appears and how your thinking is surfaced, from stronger
thumbnails to clearer insights and more consistent visuals.

Take a few minutes to explore the new features and see how small
refinements can elevate your portfolio. ✨

👉 Explore the February updates ( https://t.dripemail2.com/c/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9._X19zPWt3aWl1dDkxbGxubjU2d3lva2lhIn0.tRi4cPI0lqrjlBzaOayBwkBPZ7mmpeZIEl5YfTtPAPc )

More improvements are already on the way, stay tuned. 🚀

Cheers,

UXfolio team 🖤

---------------------

address book or whitelist us. Want out of the loop? https://t.dripemail2.com/c/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9._ZD15Y3J3c3V4ODd6eDh1Z3U4M3NvZyZleGNsdWRlX2NsaWNrPTEmX19zPWt3aWl1dDkxbGxubjU2d3lva2lhIn0._jgWxy9J2ugwA4iZZQXwuxPvQ1oNtdomXJxcY74IEy0

subject: Meet the Newest Amazfit Trailblazers
body_text:
We’re excited to welcome two of trail running’s fiercest competitors — Ruth Croft and Rosa Lara Feliu — to Team Amazfit.

[Ruth Croft](https://us.amazfit.com/pages/ruth-croft)

https://us.amazfit.com/pages/ruth-croft

[Ruth Croft](https://us.amazfit.com/pages/ruth-croft) brings her intentional, performance-driven approach to the [T-Rex 3](https://us.amazfit.com/products/amazfit-t-rex-3) and [Helio Strap](https://us.amazfit.com/products/helio-strap), using precise training and recovery insights to stay strong through high-mileage weeks and mountain terrain.

[Rosa Lara](https://us.amazfit.com/pages/rosa-lara-feliu)

https://us.amazfit.com/pages/rosa-lara-feliu

[Rosa Lara](https://us.amazfit.com/pages/rosa-lara-feliu) Feliu trains with the [T-Rex 3](https://us.amazfit.com/products/amazfit-t-rex-3) and [Helio Strap](https://us.amazfit.com/products/helio-strap), pairing instinct with data to fine-tune her recovery, manage effort, and prepare for every climb with confidence.

body_text:
To view this email as a web page, go to the following address: https://info.mongodb.com/index.php/email/emailWebview?mkt_tok=MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgxSO8tZdp-P1W6OLrvzvjlJ9Td8renC0Ksd0yGEK9ZU9LFFoCfpLLXtH0q0O4tcRQzqoJ4apKPIaGy2000Py0jAHFvdsHsLE-nTzclz6y6qihdw 

Hi Jasmin,


The fourth session of our series, RAG with MongoDB and Python, is now available to watch on-demand.

Join us for the series finale on April 1 at 11am ET, Agents with MongoDB and 
Python <https://em.mongodb.com/MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgxSO8tX1Rj72NWcOBNGlr1GUCKu-EzED5wA1WnE2pRdoIapGPNyBg-Xtea_5-0C15R4xdDlQ=>, where we bring everything together to develop autonomous AI agents powered by LangGraph and real-time database orchestration.


	- Learn how to leverage MongoDB for real-time data management and seamless database orchestration to enhance AI agent workflows.
	- Discover how LangGraph simplifies the integration of Python-based autonomous agents with MongoDB to build intelligent, scalable systems.
	- Gain hands-on insights into creating fully functional AI agents equipped for decision-making and adaptability.



MongoDB experts will be available for 1:1 support to help you troubleshoot issues and answer your questions in live time as we go through hands-on challenges. 

Additionally, you’ll have another opportunity to earn a MongoDB Skill Badge during the workshop that you can add to your LinkedIn profile to showcase your expertise in modern data architecture. 

If you want to catch up on Part 4: RAG with MongoDB and 
Python <https://em.mongodb.com/MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgxSO8tUHOwoUlLX5dDGeMFhD-b0BdbcKzdBNGZ2t7L_nbhIaNzhWkZh0RcfA3qjHnaE0X-_k=>, the recording is now on-demand. You can also still complete the corresponding Skill 
Badge <https://em.mongodb.com/MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgxSO8tdVIIJN5IQhOARcqa-td_hWvaALm_6Hvuua_cNujBBzypzxeH4Iy1uouCwUiLvPo6WU=>.

Ready to start building autonomous AI agents?
Register now <https://em.mongodb.com/MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgxSO8tfX4OVX8zD_WHEIqblqSNCcv3c-9LybtIrlUhlNoyj4A70GDbpjJxaJfJ5LnPOJX0D0=>
Think Big, Go Far,
The MongoDB Team

subject: From Kitchen to Community – Sell Pies, Change Lives
from_name: Pie In The Sky at Community Servings
body_text: Email from Community Servings You’ve helped nourish our neighbors—now help us reach even more.       Dear Jasmin: Thanks to your incredible support in the kitchen, thousands of neighbors living with critical and chronic illnesses have received the nourishing meals they need. This fall, we invite you to take that impact even further—by becoming a volunteer pie seller for our annual Pie in the Sky fundraiser. Right now, over 300 people are on our waitlist, hoping for a spot in our meals program. These are our neighbors—many living with serious illnesses—and they’re counting on us. Pie in the Sky is a Thanksgiving tradition where every apple, pecan, or pumpkin pie sold provides a full week of medically tailored meals to someone too sick to shop or cook for themselves. It’s a simple, powerful way to support our meals program—and you don’t need any sales experience to make a difference. Why Sell Pies? 🥧 One Pie = One Week of Meals 🧡 Mobilize Your Personal Network for Good 🌟 Be Part of Something Bigger Amid Uncertainty Volunteer Benefits An exciting Pie Kick-Off Party on 10/9 at High Street Place Food Hall No fundraising minimums Sell solo or create a team Make a real impact—one pie at a time Seller registration is open. Pies are available for purchase beginning October 1, with pickup at over 40 locations across Eastern Massachusetts on Tuesday, November 25!   SIGN UP TO MAKE A DIFFERENCE   Join us for a Pie Kick-Off Party at High Street Place Food Hall! We’re kicking off this year’s Pie in the Sky campaign with a celebration at High Street Place Food Hall—a vibrant hub of local food and community in downtown Boston! 📅 Thursday, October 9 | 🕕 6–8 p.m. 📍 High Street Place Food Hall - 100 High St. Boston, MA 02110 Join us for an inspiring evening where you’ll: Connect with fellow pie sellers—new and seasoned Pick up expert tips and promotional materials Enjoy delicious bites from High Street’s incredible vendors Get energized to make a real difference this season Whether you're a first-time seller or a longtime supporter, this event is the perfect way to launch your campaign and experience the power of community in action. JOIN THE PIE KICK-OFF PARTY!     Community Servings | 179 Amory Street | Jamaica Plain, MA 02130 US Unsubscribe | Update Profile | Constant Contact Data Notice

subject: Thanks for your interest in eBay! What's next?
body_text: Hi Jasmin, Great news! After reviewing your profile, eBay would like to move forward with next steps for the position: 2026 User Experience Researcher Intern . What does this mean for you? This means recruiters have reviewed your resume and application and deemed that you may be a fit for a role with one of the Hiring teams. They have forwarded your resume/applications to the teams that are hiring for this role. If there is interest from the Hiring teams, then one of their recruiters will be in touch with next steps. Please note , this is not a guarantee of an interview. Keep an eye out for additional emails (check your spam) about next steps in the process with eBay. Best, Zach

subject: 85,000 bonus points: Your exclusive welcome offer
body_text: Enjoy even more travel benefits with the Chase Aeroplan® Card. Enjoy even more travel benefits with the Chase Aeroplan® Card. Web version 0 pts + Hello Jasmin, Fly to Canada or another continent with 85,000 bonus points As a new cardmember, you can earn 85,000 bonus points after spending $4,000 in the first 3 months from account opening. ** That’s enough to fly to Canada or another continent. Your welcome bonus of 85,000 points can be worth $1,062 when redeemed for travel statement credits with Pay Yourself Back ® . ** Learn more Enjoy your day of travel even more with these built–in card benefits. Free First Checked Bag ** Cardmembers and travel companions (up to 8) traveling on the same reservation will all get free first checked bags (up to 50 lbs.) when travel originates on an Air Canada ® flight. Global Entry or TSA PreCheck ® or NEXUS Fee Credit ** Receive a statement credit of up to $120 every 4 years as a reimbursement for the application fee charged to your Chase Aeroplan ® card. Learn more Apply by April 29, 2026 ** Offer details | † Pricing and Terms $95 Annual Fee † This credit card is available to you if you do not have the Chase Aeroplan ® Card and have not received a new Cardmember bonus for the Chase Aeroplan Card in the past 24 months. Update Profile | FAQ | Terms and Conditions Contact us | Privacy Policy | Web version You have been sent this email because you are subscribed to receive Aeroplan promotional communications via email. If you no longer wish to receive them, you can unsubscribe . + The Aeroplan points balance displayed in this email may not accurately reflect your current points balance. To view your points balance, account activity and more, please visit your Aeroplan dashboard. Please do not reply to this email. Mailing address: Aeroplan Centre, P.O. Box 24000, Station Pointe‑Claire Dorval, Pointe‑Claire (Quebec) Canada H4Y 1K4. Learn more about Aeroplan's 18‑month inactivity policy on our website at aircanada.com/aeroplan‑inactivitypolicy . **Offer Details: Offers may vary depending on where you apply, for example online or in a branch, and can change over time. To take advantage of this particular offer now, apply through the method provided in this advertisement. Review offer details before you apply. 85,000 Bonus Points After You Spend $4,000 On Purchases In The First 3 Months From Account Opening: This product is not available to either (i) current cardmembers of the Chase Aeroplan Card, or (ii) previous cardmembers of the Chase Aeroplan Card who received a new cardmember bonus for this card within the last 24 months. To qualify and receive your bonus, you must make Purchases totaling $4,000 or more during the first 3 months from account opening. (“Purchases” do not include balance transfers, cash advances, travelers checks, foreign currency, money orders, wire transfers or similar cash‑like transactions, lottery tickets, casino gaming chips, race track wagers or similar betting transactions, any checks that access your account, interest, unauthorized or fraudulent charges, and fees of any kind, including an annual fee, if applicable.) After qualifying, please allow 6 to 8 weeks for bonus points to post to your account. To be eligible for this bonus offer, account must be open and not in default at the time of fulfillment. Use Aeroplan Points With Pay Yourself Back ® : Aeroplan Points may be redeemed for a statement credit using Pay Yourself Back toward eligible purchases made with your Aeroplan card within 90 days from the purchase date. Categories, including promotional categories, eligible merchants, and purchase transaction eligibility may change from time to time. Redemption values will be shown on the transaction page prior to redemption. Redemption values may be changed at any time. We may apply a maximum amount of points you can use with Aeroplan points redemption with Pay Yourself Back from time to time. Statement credits will post to the card account within 3 business days of a request to redeem and will appear on the monthly Chase credit card billing statement within 6 to 8 weeks. Statement credits will reduce your balance, but you are still required to make at least your minimum monthly payment. Chase reserves the right to determine which purchases qualify for a statement credit. Only Aeroplan Points earned under the Aeroplan Program, the Chase Aeroplan Card, and Chase Ultimate Rewards ® can be used for Chase Pay Yourself Back. Points converted from other programs are not eligible. For information about Chase rewards categories, see chase.com/RewardsCategoryFAQs . If Aeroplan determines, in its sole discretion based on its data, that you have redeemed ineligible Aeroplan Points, Aeroplan reserves the right to reverse your point redemption or freeze your Aeroplan Membership account. You will be responsible for any balance on your credit card account resulting from a reversal. Free First Checked Bags You, as the primary cardmember, and up to eight (8) other passengers traveling on the same reservation (up to a maximum of nine (9) travelers), are each entitled to a free first checked bag up to 50lb. Benefit only applies when checking in with Air Canada, for a flight operated by Air Canada, Air Canada Rouge ® or under the Air Canada Express ® brand. Free first checked bag benefit is applicable only when the bag is checked in at the designated check–in counter, prior to security. Bags checked in at the gate are not eligible for this benefit. Benefit is not available if check–in is with another airline. If the first checked bag is already complimentary (for example, as a result of Aeroplan Elite ® Status or fare purchased), there is no additional checked bag benefit that will be provided. Free first checked bag benefit may not be applied retroactively, and no refunds will be issued. Service charges for additional/oversized/overweight baggage may apply. Chase is not responsible for the provision of, or failure to provide, the stated benefits. For more information on baggage restrictions, please visit aircanada.com/baggage . Aeroplan 25K Status for New Cardmembers You, as the primary cardmember, will receive Aeroplan 25K Status for the calendar year in which your Chase Aeroplan Card account is opened and for the following calendar year. If you have earned a higher status by other means (in accordance with Air Canada’s Aeroplan Elite Status Terms and Conditions), you will retain the higher status. This benefit is not available to current or previous cardmembers who received this benefit of the credit card within the last 60 months. Aeroplan 25K Status and access to all associated features, benefits, services and amenities are subject to the Terms and Conditions of the Aeroplan Elite Status program and are available at aircanada.com/elite-termsandconditions . Aeroplan 25K Status is non transferrable. Your Chase Aeroplan Card account must be linked to your Aeroplan number and must be open and not in default to receive and retain Aeroplan 25K Status. Chase is not responsible for the provision of, or failure to provide, the stated benefits. Global Entry or TSA PreCheck ® or NEXUS Application Fee Statement Credit You will receive one statement credit every four years (up to $120) after the first program (either Global Entry or TSA PreCheck ® or NEXUS) application fee is charged to your Chase Aeroplan Card, by you or an authorized user. This benefit applies only to the Global Entry, TSA PreCheck ® or NEXUS programs, other Trusted Traveler Programs are not eligible. Only purchases made directly with the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, eligible partner listed on ttp.cbp.dhs.gov , or authorized enrollment providers featured on tsa.gov/precheck website are eligible for reimbursement. Purchases made through any third parties, such as travel agencies or application assistance services, are not eligible for reimbursement. The statement credit will appear on your credit card billing statement within 1–2 billing cycles. You are responsible for payment of all charges until the statement credit posts to the account. Chase has no control or liability regarding these programs including, but not limited to, applications, approval process or enrollment, or fees charged by CBP or TSA or DHS. For more information about the Global Entry, TSA PreCheck ® and NEXUS programs, including application details and full terms and conditions, go to ttp.cbp.dhs.gov . Websites and other information provided by government agencies are not within Chase’s control and may not be available in Spanish. To receive statement credits, your account must be open and not in default at the time of fulfillment. TSA PreCheck ® is a registered trademark and is used with the permission of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security. Over 1,300 Destinations : Number of destinations based on the published route network of Air Canada and its airline partners. Mastercard, the circles design, World Mastercard and World Elite Mastercard are trademarks of Mastercard International Incorporated. AEROPLAN PROGRAM INFORMATION The Aeroplan number of the person accessing the benefit must be included in the qualifying reservation, and the name on the airline reservation must be identical to the name on the Aeroplan account of the traveler. Please allow up to 72 hours after the Chase Aeroplan Card is approved for these benefits to be activated. Your Aeroplan account must be in good standing at time of flight for airline benefits to apply. Airline benefits will no longer be available upon Aeroplan account closure, regardless of reason for closure, or if the credit card product is changed. Aeroplan membership and benefits are subject to the Aeroplan Program Terms & Conditions and any applicable Air Canada terms and conditions relating to a benefit, as determined by Air Canada in its sole discretion and as may be changed from time to time. Chase is not responsible for the provision of, or failure to provide, the stated benefits. Air Canada ® is a registered trademark of Air Canada used under license by Aeroplan Inc. Aeroplan ® is a registered trademark of Aeroplan Inc., used under license. Chase Aeroplan credit cards are issued by JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. Member FDIC. Accounts subject to credit approval. Restrictions and limitations apply.

subject: Your October News Bite
from_name: Pie in the Sky at Community Servings
body_text: Email from Community Servings Support Our Meals Program by Selling Pies This Fall.       Right now, over 200 critically ill neighbors are waiting for the meals they need. You can help us serve them sooner and help us reach our $1M fundraising goal—one pie at a time. Join us as a Pie Seller for Community Servings’ 33rd annual Pie in the Sky fundraiser. It’s more than a Thanksgiving tradition—it’s a life-changing campaign that turns your network into nourishment for people who are too sick to shop or cook. Why Sell Pies? 🥧 Every $35 pie = a week of medically tailored meals 🧡 No fundraising minimums—just maximum impact 👥 Sell solo or build a team 🌟 Be part of a movement that’s raised millions to support our programs Whether you sell 5 pies or 50, you’ll help us be there for neighbors who are counting on us. Of course, it's never too early to order pie, too! Click here to order your favorite Thanksgiving pie(s) through Saturday, November 22! We’re proud to be supported by our generous lead sponsors: America’s Test Kitchen, Coldwell Banker Realty Cares Foundation, High Street Place Food Hall, Income Research + Management, ScrubaDub Auto Wash Centers, and Tito’s Handmade Vodka, with additional support from Boston magazine, Signature Boston, Boston Baking Inc., Big Foot Moving & Storage, and Clear Channel Outdoor. Ready to make a difference? SIGN UP AS A PIE SELLER GIVE BACK. GET PIE. And don’t miss our Kick-Off Party on Thursday, October 9 at High Street Place Food Hall. Details below! 👇🏻👇🏼👇🏽👇🏾👇🏿   We’re kicking off this year’s Pie in the Sky campaign with a celebration at High Street Place Food Hall—a vibrant hub of local food and community in downtown Boston! 📅 Thursday, October 9 | 🕕 6–8 p.m. 📍 High Street Place Food Hall - 100 High St. Boston, MA 02110 Join us for an inspiring evening where you’ll: Connect with fellow pie sellers, new and seasoned Pick up expert tips and promotional materials Enjoy delicious bites from High Street’s incredible vendors Get energized to make a real difference this season Whether you're a first-time seller or a longtime supporter, this event is the perfect way to launch your campaign and experience the power of community in action. JOIN THE PIE KICK-OFF PARTY Our Volunteer Program Needs Your Help! We need more kitchen volunteers to join us in Jamaica Plain for the following shifts: Monday, October 6, at 1 pm and 4 pm Friday, October 10, at 9 am and 1 pm Monday, October 20, at 9 am 🙌 Please sign up to volunteer with us! Take the Volunteer Experience Survey Over 90 dedicated volunteers have completed our Volunteer Experience Survey. Now it's your turn! Let us know how we can make our exceptional volunteer program even better. The survey is anonymous and takes about 5 minutes. We're excited to hear your feedback! TAKE THE SURVEY Win a Table for Four at a French Feast Honoring Jacques Pépin! Enter our giveaway for a chance to attend an unforgettable dinner on Thursday, November 13, celebrating Jacques Pépin’s 90th birthday and supporting Community Servings’ Teaching Kitchen. How to Enter: Anyone can enter! We suggest a $50 donation per entry to support the Teaching Kitchen, our culinary job-training program, but no donation or purchase is required. The Experience: Enjoy a French-inspired menu prepared by Teaching Kitchen trainees and graduates under Chef Eric Spitz. While Chef Pépin won’t be in attendance, his legacy will be honored through timeless dishes. Menu Highlights: Chicken Liver Mousse with toasted baguette and fall salad Beef Daube with pomme purée and glazed carrots or Fall Vegetable Risotto French Cheese Course with preserves and crostini Dessert by Teaching Kitchen graduate and Pastry Chef Alexa Ortiz Four lucky winners will each receive a table for four to enjoy with three guests. The drawing will take place on October 15. ENTER THE GIVEAWAY What’s Changing With SNAP, Medicaid, and the ACA? We want to make sure you're informed about recent changes to SNAP, Medicaid, and the Affordable Care Act, and how these changes will impact us in Massachusetts. Learn what policy experts are saying—and what actions can help mitigate harm. 👉 Read our blog post here. Key Takeaways: New paperwork requirements will make it harder for people to access SNAP and MassHealth, even when they qualify. Massachusetts will have to shoulder new administrative and benefit costs of SNAP New work requirements and more frequent eligibility redeterminations are estimated to cause up to 203,000 Massachusetts residents to lose MassHealth As the pressure grows on the Commonwealth's budget, we need to speak up about our mission and the programs that support it! READ OUR LATEST BLOG DAF Day Is Coming. Amplify Your Impact on October 9. Donor-Advised Funds (DAFs): Simple, Powerful, and for Everyone. A DAF is one of the easiest and most tax-smart ways to give. With just a few steps—often through your financial advisor or investment platform—you can start supporting causes you care about, like Community Servings. DAFs are: ✅ Easy to set up ✅ Tax-efficient ✅ Flexible and impactful Whether you're donating cash, stocks, or real estate, your contributions grow tax-free while you recommend grants to nonprofits over time. DAFs aren’t just for major philanthropists—they’re for anyone who wants to make giving part of their financial strategy. We’ve seen an increase in donors utilizing DAFs to support our mission of delivering medically tailored meals to individuals and families facing illness and food insecurity. Whether you're new to DAFs or already using one, this giving tool is a powerful way to deepen your impact and sustain meaningful change. This DAF Day, October 9, consider: Recommending a grant to Community Servings Talking to your financial advisor about starting a DAF, or Making a direct donation below Thank you for being part of this movement. LEARN MORE Thank You to Our Recent Corporate and Foundation Supporters We’re proud to share that Community Servings has received a $100,000 grant from the Boston Foundation’s Meeting the Moment: Sustaining Families initiative. This vital funding helps expand our medically tailored meals program at a time when food insecurity is on the rise and federal support is uncertain. We're also proud to recognize: Arthur F. Blanchard Trust Mirick, O'Connell, DeMallie & Lougee LLP Marriott Daughters Foundation Your generosity enables us to continue providing life-changing meals to those who need them most!     Community Servings | 179 Amory Street | Jamaica Plain, MA 02130 US Unsubscribe | Update Profile | Constant Contact Data Notice

March 11, 2026

Designing without borders: How are agencies are still scaling to global studios?
Designing without borders:

How are agencies are still

scaling to global studios?

 
As creative agencies expand into new cities and regions, the challenge is no longer just opening offices, it’s building cultures that balance global perspective with local relevance. From London to Singapore to Saigon, leading studios are discovering how geography, collaboration, and cultural nuances are reshaping creative work.

Also in this issue
* How ethnography is shaping the next generation of designers
* Run, draw, repeat: A crowdsourced marathon map raising funds for Oxfam
* Designing their own paths: Women in the Dribbble community share their stories

 

Inside the new wave of international design studios

Even in today’s economy, design studios are prioritizing expansion to new global markets with a clear focus: blending international reach with local cultural understanding. LePub’s London launch combines startup energy with the backing of a global network, while Porto Rocha’s London studio extends its remote-first collaboration across continents. Gut’s new Singapore office merges Latin American creative boldness with Asian cultural nuance, creating work that resonates regionally. Meanwhile, BaseSGN in Saigon is building on the legacy of Rice Studios while connecting Southeast Asian talent to a global design network.

Across all four examples, expansion isn’t simply about scale. It’s about prioritizing diverse teams to hone regional flair and allowing creative identity to evolve through cultural exchange.

Dynamic Filters for CMS now in Framer

Framer is the no-code website builder that helps designers build and launch websites lightning fast. With new features like Dynamic Filters for CMS ( https://email.n.dribbble.com/c/eJy0kk2OnDAQhU9TbNC0_IeBBYtJI6RscgVk7JpuT7CNbNOTuX1EDyTkANmhV58ez69KK7coe_NQfTs-R2ug6jvKG0EZLU4EOmXnMa3TO-q8MTAQaAdortASuDJ4Jd99sgbLfMfS469cfqgHluGtvM1hUnNpMNmbL1NejQ3p7L3EsLmOXjncrPtop2ma8cxE1Hax6PNoglPWb9xty3TRwZ3B_xMxo1tmlfFPxn-Gn8tT-4EfacacMZ6nDxWtyjY8I1-DzzHMhemMZDWTBXa0rjmrRF1Xxb1jaBpN8U1rIinXTaUkSomaN9PUCkEL2zHCJOGU0kZIWl0aMbWVFESo-k0IWoMg_mL2Bp_lzN095yUBfwU2ABtMnOaL9cCGn8CGw2786iaOQ1QO43gNyyfwYc1uTGGNGoH3D4wBmNw0h8auDnj_PIxd1MFn9Bl4r7_eeehHG7w_fgesYvs64k5ljJvhqcXYvavkrDeEtCDI333nbovyst_pC61oQ2m7y8WjY78DAAD__1ZK7n4 ), designers unlock advanced filtering with Search, Checkboxes, Toggles, Dropdowns, and more all without any code. Building a site has never been easier and now designers can become Certified Framer Experts on Dribbble. Start building with Framer today.

Why design ethnography is really about human skills

As our designs are increasingly shaped by AI and automation, design ethnography highlights the skills that remain deeply human. Teaching at the University of Michigan, Sheng-Hung Lee explores how ethnographic methods cultivate empathy, contextual thinking, and creative confidence among emerging designers. Through fieldwork, interviews, and collaboration with industry partners like GM, students are learning to interpret lived experience rather than simply apply tools. This practice reframes design not just as problem-solving, but as a relational discipline that combines listening, reflection, and human understanding.

Turning the London Marathon into a living illustration

Illustrator Dan Woodger is combining endurance and illustration in Run London/Draw London, a participatory art project tied to the London Marathon. For every £5 donation to Oxfam, Woodger adds a custom character to a massive illustrated map of the marathon route. The resulting cartoon map is a playful, ever-growing artwork shaped by the greater running community. The project turns each supporter into part of the final piece by blending crowdfunding, storytelling, and illustration; proof that creativity and community can move together for a meaningful cause.

subject: Recent cybersecurity incident
body_text:
https://view.hu.harvard.edu/?qs=587828fe5cd42e0e06cc57c225bd54f18f0e1695bf3366464d672769ca99a95d2d9b847ea3782b88950825aa620560ced817c2a8195de9b855d93b0a1b63864e76c526140a833b19d5bd65f4fe3e9ae19d492cc3e16c3221 
View this email in your browser .


 
 


 

 
 

 Dear Jasmin,


On Tuesday, November 18, 2025, Harvard University discovered that information systems used by Alumni Affairs and Development were accessed by an unauthorized party as a result of a phone-based phishing attack. The University acted immediately to remove the attacker’s access to our systems and prevent further unauthorized access.


We are writing to make you aware that information about you may have been accessed and so you can be alert for any unusual communications that purport to come from the University. Though the information systems that were accessed do not generally contain Social Security numbers, passwords, or financial account numbers, they do include personal information such as email addresses, telephone numbers, home and business addresses, event attendance, and details of donations to the University.


We take the privacy and security of your data very seriously. At this time, we do not know precisely what information was accessed. We are working with third-party cybersecurity experts and law enforcement to investigate this incident, and any additional information and relevant updates will be available 
https://click.hu.harvard.edu/?qs=2fe09d9311e9d75f5643303d5e6d80cba34cb67a67c9939eaa79829cebec0e2515cc666b29b0a5492f7270260b2162c0a66121d09076c41704babc15411e0084 
on this website .


Sincerely,

subject: Top 5 Half-Marathon Training Tips
body_text:
[Top 5 Half-Marathon Training Tips](https://us.amazfit.com/blogs/blog/grant-fishers-top-5-half-marathon-tips)

[Top 5 Half-Marathon Training Tips](https://us.amazfit.com/blogs/blog/grant-fishers-top-5-half-marathon-tips)

As 2× Olympic medalist Grant Fisher prepares for his half-marathon debut at the United Airlines NYC Half, his training has shifted from the speed of the track to the endurance demands of 13.1 miles.

We caught up with Grant to talk about how he’s adapting his training and what runners should focus on when preparing for a half marathon.
 
Here are five key lessons from his approach:

- Build mileage gradually
- Trust the power of consistency
- Make strength training part of your routine
- Prioritize longer threshold workouts
- Protect your recovery
Whether you're training for your first half marathon or chasing a new personal best, Grant’s approach focuses on patience, consistency, and listening to your body.

subject: Celebrate Jacques Pépin’s 90th with a French Feast for a Cause
body_text: Email from Community Servings Support the Teaching Kitchen & Enter to Win a Seat at the Table!     Celebrate Jacques Pépin’s 90th with a French Feast for a Cause Support the Teaching Kitchen & Enter to Win a Table! Join us on Thursday, November 13, for an unforgettable evening honoring the 90th birthday of legendary chef and philanthropist Jacques Pépin and supporting the Teaching Kitchen at Community Servings, a transformative culinary training and job readiness program. Jacques Pépin and the Jacques Pépin Foundation have long supported culinary education and the mission of the Teaching Kitchen. This special dinner directly benefits the program, empowering aspiring chefs with the skills and confidence to build meaningful careers. The Experience Enjoy a French-inspired menu prepared by Teaching Kitchen trainees and graduates under the expert guidance of Chef Eric Spitz. While Jacques Pépin won’t be in attendance, we will celebrate his legacy through timeless dishes crafted in his honor. Menu Highlights Include: Chicken Liver Mousse, toasted baguette, frisée, radicchio, and fennel salad Beef Daube, pomme purée, glazed carrots or Fall Vegetable Risotto French Cheese Course, preserves, dried and pickled fruits, crostini Dessert Course by Teaching Kitchen graduate and Omni Boston Hotel Seaport Pastry Chef Alexa Ortiz JOIN US! Win a Table With Three Guests of Your Choice Each entry is a suggested donation of $50 and enters you into a promotional drawing for one table of four at this exclusive dinner. Four winners will receive this giveaway. However, no donation or purchase is necessary to enter or win. Winners may invite three guests of their choice and enjoy an unforgettable evening of French cuisine and fine wine inspired by Chef Pépin and prepared by Teaching Kitchen trainees and graduates under Chef Eric Spitz. subject: State Senator Dr. Aisha Wahab: FREE EVENTS
body_text: My team and I are hosting several free events to support and engage our community-we hope you can attend. Hi Neighbor, My team and I are hosting several free events to support and engage our community-we hope you can attend. Our Career Fair is a great opportunity to meet local employers and explore job opportunities right here in our district; join us on Friday June 27th from 10 am- 2 pm at Chabot College . Register here : State Senator Dr. Aisha Wahab and Alameda County Supervisor Elisa Marquez's Career Connections Fair. Learn more about your rights and resources available at our FREE Virtual Know Your Rights Town Hall on Wednesday July 2nd from 5 pm- 7 pm . Register here : Join us on Saturday, July 12 from 9 am to 12 pm for our Community Clean-Up at the Hayward Shoreline . Come for as long as you're able-your support helps keep our shoreline clean and vibrant! Register : Opportunity Details We hope you'll join us and be part of the continued effort to support and strengthen our district. If you have any questions please call my office at 510-794-3900. Hi Jasmin, 

Definitely don't want to pester you, so this is my last email to you.  

I know you probably get a lot of emails, but I specialize in working with mid-career professionals and helping them get hired faster for their next, most fulfilling role.  

My process is battle-tested (laid out for you step by step) and has worked for my clients, and it will also work for you too. 

If you follow my process, you will get results.  

This is my last email.  

Now’s the time to make a change and take a different approach.  

If you do the same thing as everyone else then you will get the same results everyone else has. 

Fast-tracking your job search and landing a new role is 100% possible. 

I’ve helped over 200 professionals shorten their timelines by landing a new role, and I can help you do the same.  

Here are some examples of our client results track record: 

 * Gilad: went from a Meta layoff with zero prospects to interviewing with 12 companies, got to the offer stage with 4, and, landed an exciting Program Manager role with significantly higher pay. Click here https://inst.careercoachdbradley.com/lt/2251799925360004/kTWAoOqKuZI6l7NMQQFgD for his case study
 * JoAnne: had over 20 years of experience and struggled to secure interviews. She landed the exact leadership role she wanted in Pharma in 90 days. Click here https://inst.careercoachdbradley.com/lt/2251799925360005/kTWAoOqKuZI6l7NMQQFgD for her case study.
 * Gustavo: landed an incredible growth role as a Finance Director, with significantly higher pay, click here https://inst.careercoachdbradley.com/lt/2251799925360006/kTWAoOqKuZI6l7NMQQFgD for his case study

 * Adi felt stuck in his mid-career journey in the banking and financial sector, struggling to break into promoted roles. With my strategy and interview prep, he secured three competing offers for higher-level positions. Click here https://inst.careercoachdbradley.com/lt/2251799925360008/kTWAoOqKuZI6l7NMQQFgD to watch his case study.



This is your last opportunity to transform your job search and career. 

Best, 
Danielle Bradley

body_text: Email from Community Servings Fresh, Flavorful, Full of Heart   Roasted Vegetables and Chickpea Salad Looking for a vibrant, nourishing dish to brighten your table? Our Roasted Vegetables and Chickpea Salad is a celebration of bold flavors and wholesome ingredients—perfect for fall gatherings or a cozy night in. It’s satisfying and packed with plant-based goodness: delicata squash, sweet potato, red onion, and fresh sage and rosemary. Plus, it comes together quickly and uses pantry staples. 🍽️ Watch the cooking demo 📖 Get the recipe START COOKING Your Support Matters More Than Ever Right now, over 200 critically ill neighbors are waiting for the meals they need. You can help us serve them sooner and help us reach our $1M fundraising goal—one pie at a time. Join us as a Pie Seller for Community Servings’ 33rd annual Pie in the Sky fundraiser. It’s more than a Thanksgiving tradition—it’s a life-changing campaign that turns your network into nourishment for people who are too sick to shop or cook. Why Sell Pies? 🥧 Every $35 pie = a week of medically tailored meals 🧡 No fundraising minimums—just maximum impact 👥 Sell solo or build a team 🌟 Be part of a movement that’s raised millions to support our programs Whether you sell 5 pies or 50, you’ll help us be there for neighbors who are counting on us. body_text: Email from Community Servings Researching Social Isolation & Loneliness Among Older Adults     Dear Jasmin, My name is Kiara, and I am working with Community Servings as part of my degree requirements at Simmons University. I am conducting an evaluation of the Community Servings volunteer program to better understand the experiences of older adults, and I’d love to hear from you! Survey Dates: March 19, 2026 - April 30, 2026 What’s Involved: A brief survey (completed online or on paper) A follow-up interview (Zoom or in person) Total time commitment: approximately 50 minutes Your Privacy Matters: Participation is voluntary, and all information you provide will be kept confidential to the extent possible by law. If you are interested in participating, please contact me at kzea@servings.org. Thank you for considering this opportunity to share your valuable experiences and help improve the Community Servings volunteer program for older adults. Warm regards, Kiara Kiara Zea Intern | The AMPL Institute Community Servings   Community Servings | 179 Amory Street | Jamaica Plain, MA 02130 US Unsubscribe | Update Profile | Constant Contact Data Notice

subject: Dreaming of Marilyn Monroe
body_text:

MoMA
# 

banner
https://link.moma.org/u/nrd.php?p=tTZXbgtp4E_298299_9666691_1_2&ems_l=11782659&i=1&d=ODc1OTI0NzA2%7CdFRaWGJndHA0RQ%3D%3D%7CNzVmYmU2OTY1MTExZmQxODE%3D%7CTUtUKy0rTmV3c2xldHRlcitHZW5lcmFsKzIwMjYwMzEyK0FydCslMkIrSWRlYXM%3D%7CMTIxMDY3NjMxOA%3D%3D%7C&_esuh=_11_a9345fcba5ac37ca2ce2a06b5f076a0a58a255431e4a1cc3a27058acb773ec8d


This year marks the centenary of Norma Jeane Mortenson, though you might
know
her as the greatest character she ever played, “Marilyn Monroe.”
Perhaps the
ultimate screen icon, Monroe still captivates because she contains
multitudes:
sex symbol, peerless comic actor, total fabrication, heartbreakingly
tragic
figure. This malleability also explains why she has inspired artists
over
generations.

For the filmmaker David Lynch, whose work famously straddles the line
between
cinema and dreams, she was a kind of muse: “You could say that Laura
Palmer [of
Twin Peaks] is Marilyn Monroe, and that Mulholland Drive is about
Marilyn
Monroe, too,” wrote Lynch. “Everything is about Marilyn Monroe.”
Dive deeper
into the Monroe/Mulholland Drive connection
https://link.moma.org/u/nrd.php?p=tTZXbgtp4E_298299_9666691_1_4&ems_l=11782659&i=1&d=ODc1OTI0NzA4%7CdFRaWGJndHA0RQ%3D%3D%7CNzVmYmU2OTY1MTExZmQxODE%3D%7CTUtUKy0rTmV3c2xldHRlcitHZW5lcmFsKzIwMjYwMzEyK0FydCslMkIrSWRlYXM%3D%7CMTIxMDY3NjMxOA%3D%3D%7C&_esuh=_11_59583b5b80f4dc48777b820e19b34716e2e6715161c0de93240508d05dc02c42
,
then head to MoMA to catch the movie—along with 13 of Monroe’s
most-loved screen
performances—in the film series Marilyn Monroe: Celluloid Dream
https://link.moma.org/u/nrd.php?p=tTZXbgtp4E_298299_9666691_1_6&ems_l=11782659&i=1&d=ODc1OTI0NzEw%7CdFRaWGJndHA0RQ%3D%3D%7CNzVmYmU2OTY1MTExZmQxODE%3D%7CTUtUKy0rTmV3c2xldHRlcitHZW5lcmFsKzIwMjYwMzEyK0FydCslMkIrSWRlYXM%3D%7CMTIxMDY3NjMxOA%3D%3D%7C&_esuh=_11_719a14a5b7dcbd457ee4a56403f03fbeb396d4346c55326045b4709bd9dfa0e1
,
opening March 12.

Andy Warhol, for whom fame and tragedy were artistic catnip, did his
best to
“canonize” the star in a series of works that all use the same
publicity photo,
including Gold Marilyn Monroe
https://link.moma.org/u/nrd.php?p=tTZXbgtp4E_298299_9666691_1_8&ems_l=11782659&i=1&d=ODc1OTI0NzEy%7CdFRaWGJndHA0RQ%3D%3D%7CNzVmYmU2OTY1MTExZmQxODE%3D%7CTUtUKy0rTmV3c2xldHRlcitHZW5lcmFsKzIwMjYwMzEyK0FydCslMkIrSWRlYXM%3D%7CMTIxMDY3NjMxOA%3D%3D%7C&_esuh=_11_445d8bb642f5b0e6515c344668dc0978ce22908b14678c60d37d6bc989a6cc49
,
which goes on view March 13 in Gallery 420 Picturing History
https://link.moma.org/u/nrd.php?p=tTZXbgtp4E_298299_9666691_1_10&ems_l=11782659&i=1&d=ODc1OTI0NzE0%7CdFRaWGJndHA0RQ%3D%3D%7CNzVmYmU2OTY1MTExZmQxODE%3D%7CTUtUKy0rTmV3c2xldHRlcitHZW5lcmFsKzIwMjYwMzEyK0FydCslMkIrSWRlYXM%3D%7CMTIxMDY3NjMxOA%3D%3D%7C&_esuh=_11_42bf97044c1349bacc74ea6d7757a10398388cd6e96c74f7b6994dc289454abf
.

it’s not
really gold

subject: Reminder: Help Community Servings Plan for our Future!
body_text:
Dear Friends,

Thank you for all that you do as a valuable member of our community. Because
of your support, our programs are more essential than ever. Last year, we
prepared and delivered more than 1.2 million scratch-made, medically tailored
meals for nearly 8,000 neighbors experiencing critical or chronic illnesses and
nutrition insecurity.

Today I’m inviting you to fill out an important survey
<https://communitycounseling.co1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3lYNzOOFFlXcagu?Q_DL=Bq2t6YxSMFSuqc5_3lYNzOOFFlXcagu_CGC_GRkacyrDkrq2z5O&Q_RD=EMD_5B20R6WDEGXnplV&Q_CHL=email>
that will help us plan for the future. Your input will shape our direction,
message, and philanthropic goals. The survey should take no more than five
minutes, and your input would be invaluable.

>From delivering hot dinners to 30 individuals in Dorchester and Roxbury 35
years ago, we’ve grown into a vital lifeline for thousands of individuals and
families. To expand our impact, Community Servings is launching an ambitious
fundraising campaign—one that will lay the foundation for the next 35 years. To
understand how we can best serve our community, we need your input!

We have engaged CCS, a local consulting firm, to help us. Your responses will
be private, and CCS will use the information to gauge interest in Community
Servings’ plan and determine our next campaign.

Your opinions and recommendations are crucial to our success. Thank you so
much for your continued partnership and support.

The e-survey will be open through the end of the day on Thursday, December
18th.


Best,

David B. Waters
CEO

Jamaica Plain, MA 02130

subject: Selling Pies, Changing Lives—Volunteer for Pie in the Sky
from_name: Pie In The Sky at Community Servings
body_text: Email from Community Servings Support Our Meals Program by Selling Pies this Fall.       Dear Jasmin: Food insecurity is on the rise across Massachusetts. Right now, 300 people—many living with serious illnesses—are waiting for nourishing meals from Community Servings. These are our neighbors, and they’re counting on us. This fall, you can help us serve more people faster by becoming a volunteer pie seller for Pie in the Sky. Pie in the Sky is our annual peer-to-peer Thanksgiving fundraiser, where every Apple, Pecan, or Pumpkin pie you sell provides a week of medically tailored meals to a neighbor who is too sick to shop or cook for themselves. It’s a simple, powerful way to make a real impact, especially during the holiday season. Why Sell Pies? 🥧 One Pie = One Week of Meals 🧡 Mobilize Your Personal Network for Good 🌟 Be Part of Something Bigger Amid Uncertainty Volunteer Benefits No fundraising minimums Sell solo or create a team Make a real impact—one pie at a time Seller registration is open. Pies are available for purchase beginning October 1, with pickup at over 40 locations across Eastern Massachusetts on Tuesday, November 25!   SIGN UP TO MAKE A DIFFERENCE   Join us for a Pie Kick-Off Party at High Street Place Food Hall! We’re kicking off this year’s Pie in the Sky campaign with a celebration at High Street Place Food Hall—a vibrant hub of local food and community in downtown Boston! 📅 Thursday, October 9 | 🕕 6–8 p.m. 📍 High Street Place Food Hall - 100 High St. Boston, MA 02110 Join us for an inspiring evening where you’ll: Connect with fellow pie sellers—new and seasoned Pick up expert tips and promotional materials Enjoy delicious bites from High Street’s incredible vendors Get energized to make a real difference this season Whether you're a first-time seller or a longtime supporter, this event is the perfect way to launch your campaign and experience the power of community in action. JOIN THE PIE KICK-OFF PARTY!     Community Servings | 179 Amory Street | Jamaica Plain, MA 02130 US Unsubscribe | Update Profile | Constant Contact Data Notice

subject: July Newsletter
body_text: July was full of energy across Senate District 10 and we were proud to celebrate, engage, and serve alongside so many of you. Hi Neighbor, July was full of energy across Senate District 10 and we were proud to celebrate, engage, and serve alongside so many of you. ⭐ Celebrating Our Communities ⭐ I was proud to join residents and local leaders at several events this month, including: Senator Wahab Celebrating Independence Day w/ Newark Fire & Community Leaders Senator Wahab touring San Jose Water Senator Wahab visit to CalFire Base Senator Wahab at the Shinn Summer Fest in Fremont Honoring scholarship recipients at the annual ANCCS Our office remains deeply committed to delivering resources and support directly to our communities. In response to growing needs across the state, we've prioritized hosting events where support is most critical, including: COMMUNITY WELLNESS FAIR Senator Wahab was proud to host an event that connected constituents to free health and wellness services. HAYWARD SHORELINE CLEAN-UP Held in partnership with the East Bay Regional Park District, Senator Wahab brought together volunteers to collect waste and help protect our shoreline and environment. Bill To Ban Higher Prices Based On Phone Data Senator Aisha Wahab has introduced a bill to prevent dynamic pricing and ban retailers from using AI and customers' phone data to increase prices. - ABC7 News SB 258 Justice for Disabled Spouses : Protects individuals with disabilities from abuse by a partner - passed committee in Assembly Appropriations. SB 262 Good Neighbor Protection Act : Supports local jurisdictions in obtaining Prohousing designations, making them eligible for state housing funding - passed committee in Assembly Appropriations. SB 259 - The Online Price Fixing Act : Prevents corporations from using information from your device to decide what price you pay. In the Assembly. SB 257 PARENT Act : establishes pregnancy as a qualifying life event, enabling uninsured pregnant people to enroll in health insurance without having to wait for open enrollment period - passed committee in Assembly Appropriations. Senior Scam Stopper in partnership with Supervisor Otto Lee's team. Berryessa Community Clean-up Know Your Rights Townhall I'm here to serve you. Thank you for staying engaged. Follow us on social media, subscribe to our updates, or attend an upcoming event, we'd love to see you there. Respectfully, Dr. Aisha Wahab State Senator, District 10 INTERESTED IN LEARNING MORE? subject: Want to Give Back this Fall? Start with Pie.
body_text: Email from Community Servings With Reduced Funding & Growing Need, Your Support Helps Deliver Healing Meals.     Give Back. Sell Pie. As fall settles in, Community Servings is preparing for Pie in the Sky, our annual Thanksgiving bake sale — and we’re inviting you to be part of it. This year, the need is urgent. Hundreds of neighbors are waiting for meals. We’re facing federal legislation that will cut SNAP and Medicaid — critical programs that many of our clients depend on. By signing up as a volunteer pie seller, you’re not just selling pies — you’re stepping up to make a difference in your community. Every pie you sell helps raise funds for scratch-made, medically tailored meals for individuals and families across Massachusetts and Rhode Island living with critical and chronic illnesses. These meals support health and healing, and each pie sold provides a full week of nourishment. Selling pies is volunteering — and it’s one of the most impactful ways to give back. Getting involved couldn't be easier. You’ll rally your friends, family, and coworkers to buy delicious, locally baked pies — apple, pecan, and pumpkin — all while sharing the mission of Community Servings. Join Us at the Pie Seller Kick-Off Party 📍 High Street Place Food Hall — Boston 📅 Thursday, October 9 | 6–8 PM 🎉 Enjoy delicious bites, drinks, and tips from veteran sellers RSVP here or email Shana Lothrop, Sr. Manager of Donor Engagement and Events: slothrop@servings.org Last year, thanks to hundreds of volunteer sellers, we raised over $1M in critical funding for our meal and nutrition programs. This year, we’re aiming even higher to ensure we can serve as many people as possible, no matter what the future holds. Will you join us? GIVE BACK. SELL PIE.   Join Us for the 14th Annual Ride for Food & 5K Walk! We’re gearing up for another exciting year of riding and walking to fight food insecurity—and we want you on our team! For the fifth year in a row, Community Servings will join Three Squares New England and more than 25 local hunger relief organizations to raise funds for medically tailored meals and support the 350,000+ individuals in Massachusetts affected by food insecurity. 📅 Sunday, October 5 📍 Noble and Greenough School, Dedham, MA 💲 Registration: $85 (Message us before Sept. 1 for a discount code!) 🚴 Riders commit to raising a minimum of $350 Whether you ride, walk, or cheer from the sidelines, your participation helps deliver life-changing nutrition to our neighbors. REGISTER FOR THE RIDE Celebrating Our 2025 LifeSavor Awardees Community Servings is proud to present the annual LifeSavor Award, a tribute to individuals whose unwavering support and dedication help advance our mission of providing nutritious meals to individuals and families living with critical and chronic illnesses. This year, at our Summer Garden Party, we had the honor of recognizing four extraordinary friends of Community Servings: Lakshmi Kailasam, Melissa MacDonnell, Lori Magno, and John Tyler. From selling Thanksgiving pies through Pie in the Sky, to volunteering in our kitchen, delivering meals, and sharing their professional expertise, these remarkable individuals embody the spirit of community service. Their kindness, empathy, and conviction remind us of what’s possible when we come together in support of our neighbors. Please join us in celebrating Lakshmi, Melissa, Lori, and John for their inspiring commitment to our mission and the clients we serve. Image Caption: Maureen Goggin, Board Secretary, LifeSavor Awardees Lori Magno and John Tyler, David B. Waters, CEO. Board Spotlight: Giles Platford on the Power of Food as Medicine In our latest blog post, we sit down with Giles Platford, President of Takeda’s Plasma-Derived Therapies Business Unit and a valued member of Community Servings’ Board of Directors, to explore how corporate partnerships can drive health equity and community impact. Giles shares insights into Takeda’s commitment to the Food is Health approach, highlighting how their support for Community Servings and the AMPL Institute is helping to deliver medically tailored meals, reduce health disparities, and build healthier, more resilient communities. From volunteer engagement to strategic investment, Giles emphasizes that supporting basic needs like nutrition isn’t just good—it’s essential for public health and long-term societal well-being. READ THE BLOG POST Stay Connected with Community Servings - Sign Up for Text Alerts! Want to stay up-to-date with the latest news, events, and urgent updates from Community Servings? Opt in to receive text alerts directly to your phone! Whether it's important announcements, volunteer opportunities, or ways you can help, our text alerts will keep you informed and connected. Sign up now to receive text updates from us: Get real-time notifications about events, campaigns, and ways to make a difference. Be the first to hear about volunteer opportunities. Stay informed on how your support is helping our community. Enter your phone number below to start receiving updates today! RECEIVE TEXT ALERTS   Make Your Legacy Count Have you considered naming a beneficiary for your donor-advised fund (DAF)? It’s an easy, tax-advantaged way to continue supporting causes you care about, long after your lifetime. By naming Community Servings as a beneficiary, your gift will help fund essential programs like medically tailored meals and nutrition services for individuals facing chronic illnesses, from cancer to high-risk pregnancies. Here’s how your legacy can make a lasting impact: ✅ Your charitable values live on ✅ No tax penalties for your contribution ✅ Simple to update your beneficiary designation in just minutes ✅ Exclusive recognition in The Bernie Smith Legacy Society Every DAF gift helps sustain our mission to provide life-changing nourishment to those who need it most. Discover more about how you can leave your legacy. LEARN MORE Thank You to Our Recent Corporate and Foundation Supporters We’re honored to announce a generous three-year, $185,000 grant from the Point32Health Foundation, the philanthropic arm of Point32Health, Harvard Pilgrim Health Care, and Tufts Health Plan. This funding will strengthen the AMPL Institute’s efforts to advance Food is Medicine through research, policy, and provider education—helping make medically tailored nutrition a core part of patient care. We’re deeply grateful to Point32Health Foundation for their investment in our mission and their commitment to building healthier communities for people of all ages. the opportunities and skills you need to have a career in IT.

different software engineering paths that match your strengths.

subject: Holiday Helpers Needed at Community Servings
body_text: Email from Community Servings Make the Season Extra Meaningful—Volunteer with Us!       Dear Jasmin, The holiday season is a time for giving—and there’s no better way to give back than by volunteering with Community Servings. One vague title might mean big consequences for designers
One vague title might mean

big consequences for

designers

 
Today, design operates at the intersection of strategy, systems, and AI-driven transformation. But many professionals are still relying on the catch-all title “UX/UI Designer.” This piece argues that these ambiguous labels don’t just blur your responsibilities, they quietly erode authority, compensation, and influence across the entire design discipline.

Also in this issue
* Getty’s punchy rebrand reimagines the power of the “G”
* Visibility by design: What you can (and can’t) control on Dribbble
* Check out new Webflow Experts for your next project

 

The ‘UX/UI’ in your bio might be holding you back

The title “UX/UI Designer” has become so broad, some feel it’s nearly meaningless. Research shows professionals using the title usually have vastly different skills, ranging from strategic research to basic wire-framing. This has been creating confusion in hiring, benchmarking, and accountability, making clarity in design roles critical as AI reshapes execution-level tasks. Leading organizations like Google, Apple, and Amazon already title roles by specialization and outcome, for example: Product Designer, Design Strategist, Design Systems Lead. And the clarity of these titles reinforce both ownership and business impact.

The main takeaway here is that titles are not just cosmetic. They shape perception, authority, and ultimately, compensation. Designers should be defining and communicating their true value with precision, not convenience.

Your Kind of Community

Dear Jasmin,

What's it like to be part of the Carnegie Mellon University community? The fact that our school color is Tartan, composed of not one hue but many, gives you a hint. No matter where you're from or what you're into, you'll be embraced and inspired here, where our differences energize us and fuel our forward motion.

body_text:
Hi Jasmin, 

Here’s a bit more context for my last message.  

I have helped over 200 mid-career professionals just over the last few months, and 90% of them didn’t know how to start getting better traction with their job search.  

They also struggled with leveraging their years of experience and lost attractive new, more fulfilling job opportunities to competitive candidates who simply knew how to sell themselves better through the hiring process.  

It’s unfortunate but true, whoever markets and sells themselves better, wins. 

Having said that - I have a proven strategy that helps professionals like you get hired faster, without wasting valuable time and energy with applications that go nowhere.  

My process worked for my client Kristen. 

She’s a talented professional who recently faced the challenging situation of being laid off from a role she had dedicated 10 years of her career to. 

After 4 months of job searching, she was taking a lot of action, but nothing was working. She turned to me for help.

Together, we worked diligently to transform her job search approach and supercharge her personal brand. And guess what? The outcome was nothing short of amazing! 

Kristen successfully secured the position of Head of Marketing Analytics and Optimization at a prominent print production company. 

She did this in 51 days after starting our work together!

She’s so excited about her new role where she’ll be blending her expertise in marketing strategy with analytics to drive outstanding results.

Curious about how we achieved this remarkable and quick turnaround? 

Check out Kristen's inspiring case study here https://inst.careercoachdbradley.com/lt/1125900016268376/3aNtWa82Ge3lY4aG07p9i.  

I’d love to connect over a quick chat to show you how to implement my method to land a new attractive role that’s aligned with your current career goals and desired lifestyle.  

Are you ready to land a new, better, more fulfilling role?  

Best, 
Danielle Bradley

body_text:
> Begin forwarded message:
> 
> From: "Design the Future" <designthefuture@dcdesignltd.com>
> Subject: Update on Design the Future 2023
> Date: February 1, 2023 at 1:12:02 PM PST
> To: "Jasmin Duong" <jasmind009@gmail.com>
> 
> 
> <https://dcdesign.lt.acemlnc.com/Prod/link-tracker?redirectUrl=aHR0cHMlM0ElMkYlMkZ5b3V0dS5iZSUyRm1ZOXgzcU10aGhN&sig=75WjhEWF8KKX8Z3qWo4LfmBrWXAxGYS9aNv9CHBt7RDF&iat=1675285937&a=%7C%7C477765057%7C%7C&account=dcdesign%2Eactivehosted%2Ecom&email=xPciLvqCMSvcuLfho%2BwLFXwFoqDlMHNmyq65fGLdufk%3D&s=bb262e5490b6450091c98c927717dde5&i=5A5A1A14>
> To My Dear Design the Future Family, 
> 
> I hope you’re all doing well as we begin a new year. I’m writing you to share some challenging news about the Design the Future program. 
> 
> What's the update?
> Unfortunately, after deep deliberation, I have to announce that we will not be hosting Design the Future in 2023 as we look for a new funding model to run the program. I’d like to give you a little context on that decision and what it means for the future of the program.
> 
> When I first launched Design the Future in 2015, it was rooted in fulfilling a dream. As I looked at our world, I saw a society riddled with false limitations. Limits that we place on the ability and capabilities of others, and a limiting belief about who should benefit most from the society and world we live in. I dreamed of breaking through the false notion that we had to accept those limitations, believing instead that those who are often overlooked for what they offer the world could come together to address challenges that weren’t being addressed otherwise. 
> 
> In that vision, those with disabilities, high school students, and college students would be the primary forces to create change, designing solutions to some of the deeply neglected, day-to-day challenges faced by our disabled community. As I set out on that journey, I was fortunate to find others who also believed in this vision and volunteered their help, (Fernanda Castelo, Nick Zirpolo, Joe Villarreal, Reba Hsu, Yi Zhang, Julia Olson, Dave Jaffe, and others like Susie Wise and Ariel Raz at the Stanford d.school in subsequent years). All of these people offering their time and assistance in the early years of Design the Future to creating a one of a kind program. Not one that was us and them, but one where able-bodied and disabled individuals worked together to ensure we were creating a better world.
> 
> As far as the funding model goes, when I first started the program I resisted seeking funding from outside entities, opting instead to fund the program through ticket sales. Design the Future was largely planned and executed by me, my executive assistant, and the consulting team at DC Design. This worked at the time because overall staffing needs were low and team was working on multiple project. 
> 
> But as both DC Design and Design the Future grew, that model became unsustainable. Despite a successful launch Design the Future: Digital into the headwind of COVID-19 in 2021, (shout out to Eliza Peters, Sarah Berner, Iliana Paz, RJ Jones, and Tony DeSylva for their support in accomplishing something we should all be proud of) our historical funding model proved infeasible for 2022 and beyond. 
> 
> And so, that brings us to the present. 
> 
> It is my goal for Design the Future to continue again one day, but for that to happen, we will need to shift to a new model that likely includes a team of volunteers and support from a foundation or donor-base. In its new form, there are several changes I would make to ensure the program can scale to impact project partners and students alike around the country. And, I would seek greater participation and planning from the Design the Future family itself. 
> 
> So with that, here’s what I can say: I don’t have any definite plans in place yet and I don’t want to make any promises, but I do still believe in what we’ve built. Design the Future has been part of my life for 8 years and its mission is as important to me today, as it was then. I still see that society riddled with false limitation, but now, I see the good that Design the Future (our work together) has done to change that. During this last 8 years, high school students, guided by their project partners and design coaches, have produced 125 functional products and apps. Some of these directly addressed problems their project partners have faced for 20 years. And while the project impact has been incredible, the human-to-human impact has been even greater. Many of the bonds that have been formed have been life-long. Students have gone into careers, launched new clubs and programs focused on accessible design because of this program. And I have no doubt that we’ve prepared a new generation of students to think more deeply about the nuances of the world they’ll be designing and the judgements they form about other people.
> 
> How you can be involved.
> If you have leads on funders that might be able to support, or would like to volunteer to lead the fundraising or program organizing effort, please reach out. For the rest of this year, I’ll be discussing possibilities with anyone who’s interested in talking about them. 
> 
> Aside from that, what I’d like to focus on right now is all of you and simply expressing my gratitude for the past 8 years of support. 
> 
> It was you that made each and every Design the Future program possible. Thank you for believing in me, each other, and the vision that this program was centered on — That we could go beyond telling kids that they can change the world, by instead showing them how. I can confidently say we did just that. Thank you for your time, energy, love, and laughter. 
> 
> If you need anything going forward, I’m still here, and if you’re interested in playing a role in shaping the future of Design the Future, please reach out. 
> 
> Thank you!
> 
> Durell

subject: Your March Recipe of the Month
body_text: Email from Community Servings A Healthy, Chocolatey Breakfast for One     Chocolate Baked Oats for One Craving something sweet for a cozy weekend breakfast—without skimping on nourishment? Meet Chocolate Baked Oats, a simple, single-serve recipe that feels like dessert but fuels you like breakfast. Blending and baking transform hearty whole‑grain oats into a soft, fluffy, cake‑like texture—completely different from stovetop oatmeal, but with the same wholesome benefits. Whole‑grain oats provide fiber to support digestion and keep you feeling full, eggs add high‑quality protein, and bananas bring natural sweetness along with potassium, an important mineral for muscle and heart health. The result? A balanced breakfast that’s easy, satisfying, and delicious. It tastes like dessert, feels like breakfast—and comes together in minutes. Enjoy as is, or top with fresh blueberries, sliced bananas, or a dollop of homemade whipped cream or a sprinkle of powdered sugar for an extra‑tasty treat. 🍽️ Get the recipe Ingredients 1 cup rolled oats 2 ripe bananas or 1 cup unsweetened applesauce 2 large eggs 2 tablespoons maple syrup 2 tablespoons cocoa powder Pinch of kosher salt Cooking spray Directions Preheat oven to 350°F. Lightly grease a ramekin or small oven‑safe pan with cooking spray. Add all ingredients to a blender and blend until smooth, about 1 minute. Pour batter into the prepared dish and bake for 20–25 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out with a few moist crumbs (not wet batter). Allow to cool in the pan for 10 minutes before serving. START COOKING   Volunteer in our Boston Kitchen! Join us Monday through Friday, at 9 a.m. or 1 p.m. Whether you’re a returning volunteer or new to our community, you’ll make an immediate impact. 👉 Sign up to help in Boston! Every day, we rely on the generosity of 100 volunteers to prep ingredients, portion meals, and pack meal bags for our clients. Volunteers are essential to our mission and the well-being of those we serve. subject: Portfolio Tip #7: Show Your Process, Not Only the Results 🧗

A conversation with Anastasia S. 
Welcome to the Creator’s Corner, a monthly chat with designers on 99d. First 
up is renowned Kiev-based designer Anastasia S, a full-service designer who 
uses hand-drawn elements to create vibrant designs with big personalities.

 With a truly unique and diverse portfolio, she prides herself as the go-to 
designer for all types of creative brands. We discuss her process, her daily 
design inspirations, and how 99d helped refine her creative voice and develop 
her skills.
   
Meet Anastasia S. 
<https://99designs.com/blog/designers/designer-anastasia-s-interview/> 



Currently working on... 
 <https://99designs.com/blog/designers/designer-anastasia-s-interview/> 

View her work 
<https://99designs.com/blog/designers/designer-anastasia-s-interview/> 





 <> 
Tell us about your design process. When I am assigned a project, I read it and 
then step away. Every brand is unique and it’s important to give yourself time 
to absorb and adjust. I create questionnaires to get a sense of what the client 
wants but also what they would like me to avoid. 
Where do you find inspiration? In Kyiv, we have a beautiful city center. The 
architecture is really cool. So I enjoy the city walks during workdays. I love 
to go on Pinterest and profiles of designers on Instagram. The more you see, 
the more ideas you get. 
How do you keep your designs fresh? I try to learn new things all the time. I 
find that it’s better to be skilled and knowledgeable across different design 
disciplines. With a diverse portfolio, I am more likely to be the go-to 
designer for small businesses and other clients.

This fall, you can make a meaningful difference by joining Pie in the Sky, our beloved Thanksgiving fundraising bake sale. subject: The Tree’s Knees
body_text:
Director’s Posts from the Collections

The Tree’s Knees
Everyone has heard of the “bee’s knees.” But what about the “tree’s knees?” Yes, just like bees, some trees have knees. The bald cypress, Taxodium distichum, native to the southeastern United States can have spectacular knees. Like the golden larch (Pseudolarix amabilis), dawn redwood (Metasequoia glyptostroboides), all larch species (genus Larix), and the Chinese swamp cypress (Glyptostroboides pensilis), the bald cypress, as the common name would suggest, is a deciduous conifer, with magnificent copper to bronze colors in the autumn (lower left image, accession 
https://click.hu.harvard.edu/?%3D%3D 
806-52*A ).
So, what are bald cypress knees? The "knees" of a bald cypress are woody upward growing protuberances of the horizontally extending root system (upper and lower right images, accession 
https://click.hu.harvard.edu/?%3D%3D 
806-52*A ). On older trees, there can be hundreds of these knees appearing above the soil (or watery bottomlands) surrounding the trunk. For well over a century, botanists have speculated (and debated) about the functional significance of bald cypress knees, but we remain uncertain. Given that bald cypresses typically live in moist to permanently water-inundated ecosystems, they may play a role in helping to oxygenate the extensive below-ground roots.


If you want to see some really great tree knees, come visit the Arnold Arboretum. We have a fantastic collection of bald cypresses, both on the Jamaica Plain end of the grounds and on Peters Hill in Roslindale. The two specimens by 
https://click.hu.harvard.edu/?%3D%3D 
Dawson Pond are easily accessible, as is the 
https://click.hu.harvard.edu/?%3D%3D 
grove in the wet seep on the east flank of Peters Hill. The most extensive set of bald cypress knees at the Arnold can be found on accession 
https://click.hu.harvard.edu/?%3D%3D 
1007-38*A (click the hyperlink for map location). Set against the snow, they are magnificent, and in the fall, how can you beat the copper-colored leaves as a backdrop?


Best wishes, William (Ned) Friedman

Director of the Arnold Arboretum

Arnold Professor of Organismic and Evolutionary Biology

Harvard University

subject: Portfolio Tip #26: Quick Portfolio Personalization in UXfolio 🌈
body_text: Hey Jasmin Duong, Take advantage of all the personalization options available under Design to make your portfolio cover page uniquely yours. Play around with the * fonts, * colors, and * project thumbnails. subject: How Well Do You Know the 1960s?
body_text: Which presidential candidates participated in the first televised debate?                                                                                                                         Home |   June 27, 2021 How Well Do You Know the 1960s? Print Collector/ Contributor/ Getty Images First Speed Limit June 27, 1652 We tend to think of speed limits as a modern convention relating to freeways and residential neighborhoods, but they actually date back much further — centuries, in fact. On this date in 1652, the Dutch colony of New Netherland (that's New York state for those of us not born in the 17th century) wrote into law that “no wagons, carts or sleighs shall be run, rode or driven at a gallop” and that anyone who did so would receive a fine of at least “two pounds Flemish,” or roughly $150. The decree related specifically to the city of New Amsterdam, the future Big Apple, whose drivers and conductors were further banned from sitting or standing on their vehicles — they were only allowed to walk alongside them, lest their horses get ahead of themselves. While those who feel the need for speed may resent them, there’s no denying that speed limits have made driving — first by horse and carriage, now by automobiles — safer for everyone, especially pedestrians. To our valued designers, 

 As we leave 2020 behind, I wanted to reflect on and celebrate the incredible 
creativity, ingenuity and kindness we’ve witnessed within the 99designs 
communityover the past twelve months 
<http://99designs.community/t/a-look-back-at-2020-and-all-that-we-have-achieved-together/328026>
.

 It has been truly inspiring to see small businesses and entrepreneurs adapt 
and reinvent themselves in the toughest of circumstances, and to support 
freelancers thriving in our strangenew world of remote work 
<https://99designs.com/design-without-borders-2020>. Thank you for trusting us 
to be a part of your creative journey and growth.

 We’re also excited to be starting a new chapter in our own journey this year 
aspart of Vistaprint 
<https://99designs.com/about/press-releases/vistaprint-99designs>. Rest assured 
the 99designs community and platform is still here for you: we’re investing 
heavily in growing our team, adding new capabilities, and building a bold new 
creative future with Vistaprint. We can’t wait to share it with you!

 As always, we love hearing your stories, suggestions and feedback so please 
feel free to send me a note atpatrickl@99designs.com 
<mailto:patrickl@99designs.com?subject=A%20note%20for%20Patrick%20> – and don’t 
forget to nominate your favourite design project of 2020 for ourupcoming 
99awards <https://99designs.com/blog/community/99awards-submissions-2021/>.

 On behalf of the whole 99designs team, we wish you a peaceful, happy and 
healthy 2021.

 Patrick Llewellyn
