body_text: Baby Ruth bars are named after what President's daughter?                                                                                                                         Home |   June 28, 2021 Test Your Sweet Tooth With These Candy Questions Adam Stoltman/ Alamy Stock Photo The Stonewall Uprising June 28, 1969 Throughout the 1960s, bars that catered to the LGBTQ+ community were frequently targeted for police raids in what was a clear act of discrimination. The Stonewall Inn on Christopher Street in New York City’s Greenwich Village was one such establishment, and one that would make history. In the early morning hours of June 28, 1969, police raided the bar, aggressively harassing, arresting, and assaulting patrons. As someone was being shoved into a paddy wagon, the person yelled to the crowd, “Why don’t you guys do something?” What followed was a six-day uprising that sparked the LGBTQ+ rights movement. The clash pitted protesters chanting “gay power” against police increasingly using violence. While tensions in the street eventually eased, the fight for LGBTQ+ liberation had just begun. The first Gay Pride parade was held the following year in New York City, and decades of Pride marches, protests, and political action followed. Thanks to these efforts, it’s now illegal to discriminate based on sexual orientation in the U.S., and the Supreme Court officially legalized same-sex marriages nationwide in 2015. Some 50 years after the Stonewall raid, the NYPD police commissioner finally admitted the raid was “wrong — plain and simple.” Today, we still celebrate June as Pride Month in remembrance of the Stonewall Uprising. Portfolio Tip #24: Keep it Together with Your Navigation Section 💆
body_text: Hey Jasmin Duong, The navigation section holds your portfolio together. To make it strong, you need to keep it clean. 🧹 But that doesn’t mean you can’t have some fun with it: ---------------------------- Edit your navigation section ---------------------------- Image * Rename the elements of your navigation by clicking the pencil icon on hover. * Add a custom link to your navigation to link to your blog, Calendly etc. * Change the font style of your navigation by clicking the palette icon on hover. ------------------------------------------- Turn on the navigation in your case studies ------------------------------------------- By default, the navigation section does not appear on your case studies. 🙈 However, you have the option to turn it on by going to Design -> Header & Footer -> Show Site Navigation. ----------- Insider tip ----------- To delete your About or Contact page from the navigation, go to those pages in edit mode and click Delete in the editor’s navbar. subject: Thank you for Design the Future 2022!
body_text:
Hi Jasmin,

Design the Future: Digital wrapped up the 2021 program with a two-week virtual schedule. We want to thank everyone who helped make Design the Future 2021 a true success! We had a fabulous group of over 100 students from across the world that came together and developed real apps in as little as two weeks.

We made many new friends, and countless virtual smiles from our students, parents and project partners kept us going strong throughout the weeks. We also had a great team of project partners, lead facilitators, coaches and interns that made all of this possible. We are very proud of all of our students who eagerly challenged themselves to design the best possible apps to improve the lives of individuals who are living with a disability.

A special thank you to all the schools, counselors, teachers and principals who recommended students to join the camp, and who promote STEM, design thinking and entrepreneurship in their classrooms.

To follow the students’ design journeys  and see their amazing apps visit: https://www.youdesignthefuture.com/app-teams-page (<https://DCDesignLTD.ontraport.com/c/s/AOG/cJ6/6/vAd/6SL/6Vjbcs/QObbwykbu/P/P/vh>) 

To stay updated with the latest news, follow us on Instagram and Facebook!

We hope you had an amazing summer and we want to wish you a fantastic 2021-2022 school year! Stay tuned for information about our 2022 programs. We are already accepting student pre-registration: https://www.youdesignthefuture.com/ (<https://DCDesignLTD.ontraport.com/c/s/AOG/cJ6/s/vAx/6SL/6Vjbcs/zQTKvjIj98/P/P/vh>) 


Thank you,
The Design the Future Team
If you wish to stop receiving our emails or change your subscription options, please visit this link:

subject: Today's Quote: "Nothing in life is to be feared..."
body_text: 16 of the Best Quotes About Fatherhood                                                                                                                         Sunday, June 20, 2021 Nothing in life is to be feared. It is only to be understood. Marie Curie Marie Curie is best known for her scientific breakthroughs in radiation and radioactivity, which won her two Nobel Prizes. Even after her husband and research partner Pierre Curie died, Marie carried on their work, introducing the first X-ray machines to the frontlines of World War I. She spoke these brave words upon discovering that her long-term exposure to radiation during her research had given her leukemia. Her rational outlook applies not just to science and mortality, but also to life: If we approach the unknown without fear, we’re more likely to gain understanding we didn’t have before. body_text: Hey Jasmin Duong, Compelling stories written in stunning fonts make for an irresistible portfolio. 🍬 So, dive into the Fonts panel of UXfolio: ------------------------------------------ Manage all your font styles from one panel ------------------------------------------ Image You can set the font styles of your portfolio in the side panel. To access the panel, just select any text in your portfolio and click the palette icon at the end of the text editing toolbar. Alternatively, you can access your font styles by going to Design -> Fonts. ------------------------- In-line text style editor ------------------------- Image Select any text in your portfolio pages or case studies and use the in-line text editing toolbar to: * change style (Headings, paragraphs, etc.), * format your text (bold, italic), * change text alignment, * add hyperlinks, * add lists, and * access the font style panel (palette icon). subject: Husky Hunt Thank You and Special Bike Deal!
body_text:
** Northeastern Husky Hunt Follow Up!
------------------------------------------------------------

Husky Hunt 2024 is officially OVER! Congratulations to all that participated in the hunt and we can’t wait for next year and to get you all on bikes again. From what we heard it sounded like a lot of fun and congratulations to the group that finished first! Here at Urban AdvenTours, we have two passions; biking and Boston. Providing bicycles to you all for the hunt fulfilled both of our passions and we are honored to be part of this amazing Northeastern tradition.

The Husky Hunt is so special to us that we wanted to offer an exclusive opportunity as a thank you. The deal is for any Northeastern student, regardless if they participated in the hunt, and as long as they have a valid student ID. Our special offer is to purchase one of our top quality Kona Dew Boston custom city bikes for only $500! These bikes are normally $850 and they come with a bottle cage, fenders, bell, 27 speeds, and hydraulic disc brakes. DO NOT miss out on this amazing opportunity and come into our shop (109 Atlantic Ave.) before December 6th to ride away in style!

Urban AdvenTours has had a good partnership with Northeastern not just during the hunt, but also as a place of work. We have had great success in the past when hiring Northeastern students. If you are interested in working with the Urban Team, you can apply here (https://www.urbanadventours.com/employment-application/) .

We really enjoyed meeting everyone this past weekend an though the hunt is over, we look forward to seeing the Huskies again next year! LET’S GO HUSKIES!!!

Sincerely,

Urban AdvenTours Team

subject: Today's Quote: "There are two ways of spreading light..."
body_text: 11 Classic Lines From the Novels of Charles Dickens                                                                                                                         Tuesday, June 22, 2021 There are two ways of spreading light: to be the candle or the mirror that reflects it. Edith Wharton This beautiful line comes from Edith Wharton’s long poem “Vesalius in Zante (1564).” The speaker of the poem is Inquisition-era anatomist Andreas Vesalius (1514-1564), who left Spain to travel to the East in his fifties, when he could no longer bear to live and work in a society that forbade his scientific research. On his way home from Jerusalem, Vesalius was shipwrecked on the Greek island of Zante, where he fell ill and died, never to return home. In the poet’s imagining, the censored scientist finds consolation at the end of his life in the faith that others will carry on the work he was prevented from: “What one man failed to speak, another finds / Another word for,” Wharton writes. In other words, carrying on the “light” of another — be it ideas, joy, love, or inspiration — can be just as valuable as creating it yourself. subject: Behind the Scenes: How an opera designer reimagined our galleries
body_text:
A “space of memory, that’s both playful and surreal”
View with images
https://link.moma.org/u/gm.php?prm=tTZXbgtp4E_872079005_9693200_52480&_esuh=_11_0b672ca0c9b9136ac593b7dd90beef1468c302107de939ba71644e8313790d97


MoMA
# 

banner
https://link.moma.org/u/nrd.php?p=tTZXbgtp4E_52480_9693200_1_2&ems_l=11826397&i=1&d=ODc4ODAxMjg2%7CdFRaWGJndHA0RQ%3D%3D%7CNzVmYmU2OTY1MTExZmQxODE%3D%7CTUtUKy0rTmV3c2xldHRlcitHZW5lcmFsKzIwMjYwMzI0K0FydCslMkIrSWRlYXM%3D%7CMTIxMDY3NjMxOA%3D%3D%7C&_esuh=_11_6200af58538c0a1870a500f5308ef30f7fe0eb58eea71b664499c1e9d6e1fd3c


What happens when the language of the stage meets the hush of the
gallery?

Jon Bausor is busy these days. On top of creating the set for the
Metropolitan
Opera’s new production El Último Sueño de Frida y Diego
https://link.moma.org/u/nrd.php?p=tTZXbgtp4E_52480_9693200_1_4&ems_l=11826397&i=1&d=ODc4ODAxMjg4%7CdFRaWGJndHA0RQ%3D%3D%7CNzVmYmU2OTY1MTExZmQxODE%3D%7CTUtUKy0rTmV3c2xldHRlcitHZW5lcmFsKzIwMjYwMzI0K0FydCslMkIrSWRlYXM%3D%7CMTIxMDY3NjMxOA%3D%3D%7C&_esuh=_11_99399169b44c23d6e05730177b56abfd06d229dfb1e6f11e9a1f4306cba15944
,
the stage and costume designer also conceived MoMA’s gallery
installation for
Frida and Diego: The Last Dream
https://link.moma.org/u/nrd.php?p=tTZXbgtp4E_52480_9693200_1_6&ems_l=11826397&i=1&d=ODc4ODAxMjkw%7CdFRaWGJndHA0RQ%3D%3D%7CNzVmYmU2OTY1MTExZmQxODE%3D%7CTUtUKy0rTmV3c2xldHRlcitHZW5lcmFsKzIwMjYwMzI0K0FydCslMkIrSWRlYXM%3D%7CMTIxMDY3NjMxOA%3D%3D%7C&_esuh=_11_9d07960dddff839577957ef71cc9d2e37d9079547046a57ae8a2dd0587278cc2
,
an exhibition celebrating two of Mexico’s most beloved icons of
20th-century
art.

We sat down with Bausor
https://link.moma.org/u/nrd.php?p=tTZXbgtp4E_52480_9693200_1_8&ems_l=11826397&i=1&d=ODc4ODAxMjky%7CdFRaWGJndHA0RQ%3D%3D%7CNzVmYmU2OTY1MTExZmQxODE%3D%7CTUtUKy0rTmV3c2xldHRlcitHZW5lcmFsKzIwMjYwMzI0K0FydCslMkIrSWRlYXM%3D%7CMTIxMDY3NjMxOA%3D%3D%7C&_esuh=_11_74220fd1754d1f72a77fdd215330d404c33e0482b78432054a3b409a3730006f

to find out more about his work across these very different spaces, the
interplay between different artforms, and what he discovered about Kahlo
and
Rivera. He takes us from first sketches to the design elements and
materials
that give the galleries their rhythm. “I’ve tried to... knit a story
together
and create an immersive experience that envelops the viewer,” says
Bausor.

Take a look behind the scenes
https://link.moma.org/u/nrd.php?p=tTZXbgtp4E_52480_9693200_1_10&ems_l=11826397&i=1&d=ODc4ODAxMjk0%7CdFRaWGJndHA0RQ%3D%3D%7CNzVmYmU2OTY1MTExZmQxODE%3D%7CTUtUKy0rTmV3c2xldHRlcitHZW5lcmFsKzIwMjYwMzI0K0FydCslMkIrSWRlYXM%3D%7CMTIxMDY3NjMxOA%3D%3D%7C&_esuh=_11_2f64cfcb1a2ffd15b910bff19bb44a54f7367eaccfb29c7ccda2e15c31476f20
,
then come to MoMA to see The Last Dream
https://link.moma.org/u/nrd.php?p=tTZXbgtp4E_52480_9693200_1_12&ems_l=11826397&i=1&d=ODc4ODAxMjk2%7CdFRaWGJndHA0RQ%3D%3D%7CNzVmYmU2OTY1MTExZmQxODE%3D%7CTUtUKy0rTmV3c2xldHRlcitHZW5lcmFsKzIwMjYwMzI0K0FydCslMkIrSWRlYXM%3D%7CMTIxMDY3NjMxOA%3D%3D%7C&_esuh=_11_abdf9af6f129250f1824a8306505e3a43883eff44f10114a704edb7b9d527c9c
.

subject: Roll the Dice With This Quiz on the History of Board Games
body_text: What is the oldest known board game?                                                                                                                         Home |   June 30, 2021 Roll the Dice With This Quiz on the History of Board Games Astronaut Robert Henry Lawrence Jr. First Black U.S. Astronaut June 30, 1967 On June 30, 1967, Robert Henry Lawrence Jr. became the first Black astronaut in America. Originally from Chicago, Lawrence graduated from high school at 16, earned a doctorate in physical chemistry from Ohio State University, and entered the Air Force by age 22. Lawrence was selected to be an Air Force astronaut, joining the Pentagon’s Manned Orbiting Laboratory (MOL) program, with a mission of putting a manned surveillance satellite in space. The program was secretive in nature, and incredibly dangerous. Pilots were often tasked with testing difficult take-offs, harrowing landings, and avoidance maneuvers. On December 8, 1967, while Lawrence was instructing another pilot on landing an out-of-control Supersonic Lockheed F-104 Starfighter, the jet crashed. While Lawrence ejected, his parachute didn’t deploy and he was killed at age 32. Although his mission was tragically cut short, Lawrence’s legacy made it to the stars. Astronauts such as Guy Bluford, the first Black American in space, and many others that followed soared into space thanks to the racial barriers that Lawrence broke. Today, Lawrence’s name is engraved in a Kennedy Space Center memorial honoring astronauts who made the ultimate sacrifice. subject: Your March News Bite
body_text: Email from Community Servings 15 Million Meals and Counting     15 Million Meals and Counting It’s official. Since 1990, Community Servings has prepared 15 million medically tailored meals for neighbors living with critical and chronic illnesses. To mark this milestone, our founder Sheila Decter—a spry and spirited 87—returned to our Boston kitchen to help package the commemorative meal. During her visit, Sheila reflected on the earliest days of Community Servings, when a small coalition of community leaders came together during the height of the HIV/AIDS epidemic to deliver hot meals to just 30 clients. What began with that small but mighty effort has grown into a regional program delivering 1.2 million medically tailored meals each year to 8,000 clients across MA and RI. This remarkable evolution speaks directly to the determination and compassion of our community. A Deeper Look Back: The StoryCorps Conversation If you’ve never heard the story of our founding, this StoryCorps interview with Sheila Decter and fellow founder Alan Balsam offers a rich, heartfelt look at our origins providing nourishment, dignity, and care to people living with HIV/AIDS. 🎧 Listen to the StoryCorps conversation: Alan Balsam & Sheila Decter – StoryCorps Archive SUPPORT OUR MEALS PROGRAM Remembering Volunteer Louis Montagut On Thursday, February 26—which would have been volunteer Louis Montagut’s 18th birthday—we dedicated the day’s meals in his honor. We reflected on the life and legacy of a remarkable young man: one of our youngest, kindest, and most devoted supporters, whose passing last fall was felt deeply across our community. That day, Louis’s classmates from Concord Academy and his father Etienne joined us in the kitchen. Together, they packaged more than 2,000 meals for neighbors living with critical and chronic illnesses — a tribute Louis would have loved. Honoring Louis Through the Louis Montagut Foundation To carry forward his spirit of compassion and curiosity, Louis’s family has established The Louis Montagut Foundation (“The Louis”) to support the causes most important to him. The Louis advances Louis’s legacy through two areas of impact: Supporting community-driven initiatives that reflect Louis’s values of empathy, creativity, and service Advancing research in the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of certain brain diseases, with a particular focus on brain edema and brain cell repair We’re honored to celebrate Louis’s life and grateful for the meaningful work being carried forward in his name. To learn more about the foundation and its mission, or to get involved, please visit: 👉 https://www.thelouis.org/ Voices From the Field: Leaders Share Their Food is Medicine Stories We’re proud to share that Community Servings’ CEO David Waters is featured in “Voices From the Field: Individual Leaders Share Their Stories of Food is Medicine,” an article including nine powerful stories from leaders across the national Food is Medicine movement and recently published in the American Journal of Lifestyle Medicine. Read the article here: https://bit.ly/4rzYyEQ Celebrate the Many Powers of Food: Join Us for LifeSavor! LifeSavor, Community Servings’ signature fundraising gala, returns on Thursday, April 30, for an unforgettable evening at the Mandarin Oriental, Boston. The celebration begins with an exquisite cocktail party for 500 guests, followed by intimate dinners hosted by Greater Boston’s finest restaurants—all in support of our mission to provide nutritious meals to neighbors living with critical and chronic illnesses. We invite guests, corporate partners, and community leaders to join us by purchasing tickets and exploring sponsorship opportunities that directly fuel our ability to nourish individuals and families facing serious health challenges. Click here to learn more and make your commitment today! We're Hiring. Join Our Mission! Community Servings is growing and we’re looking for passionate, mission‑driven individuals to help expand our impact through medically tailored meals and nutrition services. We’ve added several new roles across the organization, including: Bilingual Client Services Coordinator Bilingual Registered Dietitian Nutritionist Campaign Manager Manager of Business Development & Outreach If you or someone you know believe Food is Medicine, these are great opportunities to make a difference in the lives of our neighbors. 👉 Explore open positions and apply today. Go the Distance for Health and Hope: Join Our 2026 ASICS Falmouth Road Race Team! Be part of one of the most iconic summer running events, the 54th Falmouth Road Race! Established in 1973, this legendary and picturesque 7-mile seaside course along the Cape Cod coast attracts Olympians, elite athletes, and recreational runners from around the world. Prefer to run closer to home? The FRR At-Home Edition lets you experience the excitement from your own neighborhood. Race Day: Sunday, August 16, 2026 Team Bibs: 13 available Fundraising Minimum: $1,600 per runner Your efforts will help fund nutritious, medically tailored meals for critically and chronically ill neighbors, providing nourishment and care when it matters most. Interested? Contact Elyse Guley, Donor Engagement & Events Coordinator, at eguley@servings.org. Celebrating Volunteer Milestones: January & February Achievements We are proud to recognize the incredible contributions of our most dedicated volunteers who reached the cumulative 500-hour milestone in January and February. Their commitment makes a lasting impact, and we’re grateful for every hour they’ve given to support our mission. 500+ Hours Anne Hurwitch Jennifer Jaruse Naomi Joress Brian Parr Shawna Vogel     Community Servings | 179 Amory Street | Jamaica Plain, MA 02130 US Unsubscribe | Update Profile | Constant Contact Data Notice

subject: What’s the key to successful teamwork while working remotely?
body_text: Unlock your teams potential from anywhere with these hints and tips canva Weekly Newsletter ********************************* Share the success ********************************* The key to success for any team is communication. All the more so when there’s physical distance involved. Luckily, the digital age has gifted us with many ways we can connect and streamline workflows—with a few simple clicks. Working remotely doesn’t mean the end of workplace structure, it just takes a little more thought and coordination. To help you and your team out, we’ve got a range of presentation templates you can use to share information and updates with ease. Level up presentations ( http://l.engage.canva.com/mps2/c/AgE/0GZcAA/t.31d/pArIVgyCS4uhPnxT2No9GQ/t23/qGMlQy50C77qMymbGTGbqDFEkhVL2cyy1sQcfC5cBqzxTlQFPT8Tbveb9mp8gWU5xqOMqzECiOL-2Biv6jxFUvmQ-3D-3D/Y9OW ) Plus, it’s worth noting that if your team is meeting on Zoom, we have plenty of fun templates for creating Zoom Virtual Backgrounds. --------------------------------- Presentation tips --------------------------------- Making a presentation with Canva couldn’t be easier. Follow these helpful tips to make a professional presentation that delivers impact from your home boardroom. 1. Choose a presentation template that suits your agenda. ----------------------------------------------------------------- 2. Then customize the slides with relevant information, data, graphs, images and even a video to grab your audience’s attention. 3. Present to the team and surprise them with the built-in shortcuts, such as pressing ‘d’ for a drumroll and ‘c’ for confetti. Make your own presentation ( http://l.engage.canva.com/mps2/c/AgE/0GZcAA/t.31d/pArIVgyCS4uhPnxT2No9GQ/t25/qGMlQy50C77qMymbGTGbqG9ldTVOnWB-2Fpyh18IVkrOoJfoh7I9vtUUP2FgoUjawQukcFglFSoVKWvkcG1vZraD11FGaFcQiuaT4MicZ3s0k-3D/GW7I ) Get your team on the same page ----------------------------------------------------------------- With our presentation templates you can easily share ideas and updates with your team. We’ve also put together a range of special ‘working from home’ templates packed with best practice hints and tips. ( http://l.engage.canva.com/mps2/c/AgE/0GZcAA/t.31d/pArIVgyCS4uhPnxT2No9GQ/t26/qGMlQy50C77qMymbGTGbqDFEkhVL2cyy1sQcfC5cBqzxTlQFPT8Tbveb9mp8gWU5kbflGGFcPDE37RDSHK40GA-3D-3D/5lXT ) ( http://l.engage.canva.com/mps2/c/AgE/0GZcAA/t.31d/pArIVgyCS4uhPnxT2No9GQ/t27/qGMlQy50C77qMymbGTGbqDFEkhVL2cyy1sQcfC5cBqzxTlQFPT8Tbveb9mp8gWU5iqEuTW3WkuJfjZ9Ee898iw-3D-3D/0PlV ) ( http://l.engage.canva.com/mps2/c/AgE/0GZcAA/t.31d/pArIVgyCS4uhPnxT2No9GQ/t28/qGMlQy50C77qMymbGTGbqG9ldTVOnWB-2Fpyh18IVkrOoJfoh7I9vtUUP2FgoUjawQukcFglFSoVKWvkcG1vZraNV5phH4rYMl5q3MTSqL50k-3D/o7Wg ) See more templates ( http://l.engage.canva.com/mps2/c/AgE/0GZcAA/t.31d/pArIVgyCS4uhPnxT2No9GQ/t29/qGMlQy50C77qMymbGTGbqG9ldTVOnWB-2Fpyh18IVkrOoJfoh7I9vtUUP2FgoUjawQukcFglFSoVKWvkcG1vZraNV5phH4rYMl5q3MTSqL50k-3D/PyRj ) See more templates ( http://l.engage.canva.com/mps2/c/AgE/0GZcAA/t.31d/pArIVgyCS4uhPnxT2No9GQ/t30/qGMlQy50C77qMymbGTGbqG9ldTVOnWB-2Fpyh18IVkrOoJfoh7I9vtUUP2FgoUjawQukcFglFSoVKWvkcG1vZraD11FGaFcQiuaT4MicZ3s0k-3D/rKBJ ) Adapt to distance learning With school closures around the world, Canva is supporting teachers, parents, and students by giving them the resources and tools they need to collaborate remotely. body_text: Which amendment granted women the right to vote?                                                                                                                         Home |   July 1, 2021 Try Your Hand at This Women’s Suffrage Quiz Mario Beauregard Beaustock/ Alamy Stock Photo Sony Walkman Goes on Sale July 1, 1979 On July 1, 1979, the first Sony Walkman went on sale in Japan for 30,000 yen, the equivalent of $150 American dollars. The legend goes that Sony’s co-founder Masaru Ibuka grew tired of packing a big cassette recorder with him on long, international flights to listen to his beloved opera. So, he had his team design a portable, stylish cassette player. It wasn’t a particularly new technology, but it was repackaged as cool and convenient. They even colored it blue-silver to match denim, a hot fashion in the late 1970s. Despite low expectations, the Walkman sold like hotcakes, and eventually the trend made its way to America. The stylish Walkman became the standard bearer for listening to music on the go and a status symbol. The device left its impression on tastemakers like Andy Warhol, Hollywood, and teenagers everywhere. Eventually, cassettes were overtaken by compact discs and the Walkman became Discman. Sony finally stopped production of its portable cassette player in 2010, nearly a decade after the release of the iPod — a device Steve Jobs once called “the 21st-century Walkman.” Try Your Hand at This Women’s Suffrage Quiz 2 Pts Question 1/10 Which amendment granted women the right to vote? 2 Pts Question 1/10 13th Amendment 17th Amendment 19th Amendment 20th Amendment FPG/ Getty Images How Well Do You Remember These Famous Advertising Slogans? subject: Coronavirus at the grocery store (petition)
body_text:
Dear fellow MoveOn member,

 Kroger is the biggest supermarket company and runs grocery chains
 including Ralph's, Harris Teeter, QFC, Smith's, Fred Meyer, and Dillons.
 They have a presence in all of our communities, and now we need to show up
 to support the workers who need paid sick leave.

 The latest coronavirus relief package to pass Congress exempts large
 corporations including Kroger and its hundreds of thousands of
 employees.^1

 [ https://act.moveon.org/go/119303?t=1006&akid=260743%2E43108413%2E7B8arH ]Sign the petition demanding paid sick leave for all Kroger employees.

 Kroger is a $26 billion company that responded to the coronavirus outbreak
 by giving employees a $25 gift card to their stores. The workers there are
 doing an amazing job supporting our communities despite this awful health
 crisis. The least Kroger can do is ensure its employees have paid sick
 leave.

 [2]Sign Nandini's petition

 As entire cities and states are seemingly shut down due to the
 coronavirus, grocery stores remain open, and we all need to continue
 putting money into our local economies. However, cashiers and workers
 stocking shelves are among those on the front lines risking their health
 to support our communities and earn their wages.

 Reports have started to come in that Kroger employees are getting sick
 from the coronavirus. But in the face of increased public criticism,
 Kroger, a $26 billion corporation, is refusing to provide paid sick leave
 for employees unless they have tested positive for COVID-19 or are placed
 in mandatory quarantine by a medical professional.^2

 Instead of taking a simple step of letting sick workers simply call in
 sick, Kroger is refusing to use its enormous power to do the right thing
 for workers.

 Shockingly, Kroger's only real attempt to show workers any recognition is
 offering them a $25 Kroger gift card for their hard work!^3

 These are serious times. We must take action in solidarity with Kroger
 workers and the millions of customers who will be put at risk if sick
 workers are showing up sick while trying to earn a paycheck.

 Please sign and share this petition.

 [ https://act.moveon.org/go/119303?t=1007&akid=260743%2E43108413%2E7B8arH ]Click here to add your name to this petition, and then pass it along to
 your friends.

 Thanks!

 –Nandini Jammi

 Sources:

 1. "White House expresses support for immediate cash payments to Americans
 as part of coronavirus stimulus package," The Washington Post, March 17,
 2020
 [ https://act.moveon.org/go/117487?t=1008&akid=260743%2E43108413%2E7B8arH ]https://act.moveon.org/go/117487?t=1009&akid=260743%2E43108413%2E7B8arH

 2. "Supermarket Sick," Popular Information, March 15, 2020
 [ https://act.moveon.org/go/117457?t=1010&akid=260743%2E43108413%2E7B8arH ]https://act.moveon.org/go/117457?t=1011&akid=260743%2E43108413%2E7B8arH

 3. "Kroger Gives Workers Gift Card Money, Not Paid Leave For All, Amid
 Coronavirus," HuffPost, March 17, 2020
 [ https://act.moveon.org/go/117458?t=1012&akid=260743%2E43108413%2E7B8arH ]https://act.moveon.org/go/117458?t=1013&akid=260743%2E43108413%2E7B8arH

 You're receiving this petition because we thought it might interest you.
 It was created on MoveOn.org, where anyone can start their own online
 petitions. You can [ https://act.moveon.org/go/116370?t=1014&akid=260743%2E43108413%2E7B8arH ]start your own petition here.

Spotting scams and staying safe


Because 99designs is a marketplace where designers and clients connect 
directly, scammers may occasionally try to impersonate others or trick people 
into sharing sensitive information.

We work continuously to detect and remove bad actors, and a few simple habits 
will help you stay protected. Jump into the 99designshelp center 
<https://support.99designs.com/hc/en-us/articles/46490309593876-Staying-Safe-from-Online-Scams>
 for tips and tricks on how to stay safe from online scams.

Tips on spotting scams → 
<https://support.99designs.com/hc/en-us/articles/46490309593876-Staying-Safe-from-Online-Scams>



Tips for staying safe on 99designs

 
<https://support.99designs.com/hc/en-us/articles/46490309593876-Staying-Safe-from-Online-Scams>



👀 Look for the "Staff" badge

Official 99designs employees will have a visible "Staff" badge on their 
profile.




✋ Verify before you click

If a 99d message asks for login info, personal details, or urgent payment, do 
not reply.Report it to us immediately. 
<https://support.99designs.com/hc/en-us/requests/new>




🔐 Payment and ID verification only happen on 99designs

Never use external forms, links, or requests to “reactivate” your account.




🙅♀️ 99designs will never ask you to pay to keep your account open

Any message demanding payment to avoid suspension is a scam.



Learn more about online safety → 
<https://support.99designs.com/hc/en-us/articles/46490309593876-Staying-Safe-from-Online-Scams>


 
<https://support.99designs.com/hc/en-us/articles/46490309593876-Staying-Safe-from-Online-Scams>

Keep your clients safe from scams

Quick safety note: All payments, files, and project communication will always

looks unusual, please message me here on 99designs or email:

 –Nick, Manny, Gabby, and the rest of the team

Hey Jasmin Duong,

What makes a UX portfolio read as junior, mid, or senior?

In this live webinar session, Joseph Louis Tan, founder of Career
Creators, will break down the six questions a hiring manager runs
through in the first 30 seconds of reviewing any portfolio, and
show what those signals look like across different levels of
experience.

Save your spot ( https://t.dripemail2.com/c/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..Pvdq5q0wfHSN2F-_rwNCwGc6fuJr_77Ooll2rHLUSOI )

Image

------------------------------
In this session, you’ll learn:
------------------------------

* the six questions that shape a hiring manager’s first read of
your portfolio
* what those questions are picking up from your portfolio
* how those signals influence whether your work reads as junior,
mid-level, or senior
* how to see the gap between your intention and the signal your
portfolio sends

----------------------------------
Want your portfolio reviewed live?
----------------------------------

Selected portfolios will be reviewed in real time using Joseph’s
diagnostic framework, highlighting the signals coming through,
where the gaps are, and how the portfolio reads from junior to
senior level.

Submit your portfolio ( https://t.dripemail2.com/c/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..bCF_YIOZ8fmDfnasN4LBU4unazdalJQ36-6fVw9ajI0 )

🎙️ About the Speaker

Joseph Louis Tan is a career coach for experienced designers and
the founder of Career Creators. He has 18 years in design across
six career pivots, from industrial design and lecturing to
fintech, app design, and Head of Product Design at ContactOut. He
is based in Singapore, holds the LinkedIn Top Voice badge since
2024, and has 39,000 followers on LinkedIn.

🕒 Time: 10:00 AM CEST | 4:00 PM SGT | 1:30 PM IST

Best,

UXfolio team 🖤

 Dear Jasmin,

Thanks for registering for a counseling session at Carnegie Mellon University!

Your counseling session will be conducted via webinar at 1:15 PM ET on Thursday, June 9, 2022.

Please note that this time is in Eastern Time (ET).

You'll receive a link to access the webinar 24 hours prior to the event. The link will also be included in a 1 hour reminder. 

Admission counseling sessions allow you to seek guidance and ask questions of the Office of Admission on things like:

 Academic preparation
 Application process and application plans
 Choosing a college/major at Carnegie Mellon
 Financial Aid
 Fine arts pre-screen/audition/portfolio process
 Getting involved at Carnegie Mellon
 Housing, dining and enrollment questions

Please take a few moments to prepare any questions you have ahead of your admission counseling session. You're welcome to invite a family member or counselor to attend the session with you.

You can also fill out our Net Price Calculator <https://www.cmu.edu/admission/aid-affordability/net-price-calculator> and we can answer any specific questions you may have about your Net Price Calculator results during the session. Please note Carnegie Mellon only offers financial aid to U.S. citizens, permanent residents and Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) students.

As a reminder, admission counseling sessions aren't evaluative, and the Office of Admission doesn't offer admission interviews.

We look forward to connecting with you!

Best regards,
Office of Admission

Count Dracula was inspired by Vlad the Impaler of Transylvania.

Arts & Culture

N either Dracula nor vampires are, strictly speaking, real — at least so far as we know — but that doesn’t mean they don’t have their basis in reality. While writing his endlessly influential novel Dracula, author Bram Stoker was inspired by Central European folklore in general and
Vlad III
https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=lolxmhlsz4q4coz3ctbb1u75szwwyo12&__stmp=smzr0z&__onlt=t&email=jasmind009%40gmail.com
 in particular, whom history often remembers by a more colorful name: Vlad the Impaler. The son of Vlad Dracul, he’s believed to have been born in Transylvania, eventually became voivode (ruler) of Wallachia (a region of Romania south of Transylvania), and more than earned his nickname by impaling his enemies. Vlad Dracul took his name when he joined the Order of the Dragon, a secret cabal of Christian knights; “dracul” is Romanian for “dragon.” As fate would have it, “Dracula” means “son of Dracul.”

Stoker
called
https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=lolxmhlsz4q4coz3ctbb1u75szwwyo12&__stmp=smzr0z&__onlt=t&email=jasmind009%40gmail.com
 Transylvania “one of the wildest and least known portions of Europe” in the book’s first chapter, an evocative description based on his research into the area and 19th-century travel literature (though the author never actually visited Romania’s spookiest region). Before falling in battle in 1476, Vlad III earned a reputation for brutality. Impalement was his favorite means of torturing and dispatching his enemies, but he was also known to decapitate, disembowel, and skin them; some claim he even dipped his bread in his victims’ blood while using their impaled bodies as morbid dinner guests. Whether such gory details are true may never be known, but it’s easy to see how he inspired one of the world’s most fearsome fictional characters.

Did you know?

Sunlight isn’t fatal to Dracula in the novel.

Although sunlight does weaken Dracula and drain him of his powers, it doesn’t kill him — nor was it fatal to any other vampire for a full 25 years after Dracula was published. The trope was actually invented in the 1922 German movie
Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror
https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=lolxmhlsz4q4coz3ctbb1u75szwwyo12&__stmp=smzr0z&__onlt=t&email=jasmind009%40gmail.com
, director F.W. Murnau’s unofficial adaptation of Stoker’s novel. Widely considered one of the best, most influential horror films ever made, the German expressionist masterwork almost passed out of existence immediately after its release. Stoker’s estate sued over the film in Germany, reportedly leading to a court ordering that all copies be destroyed. Fortunately, enough prints survived for Nosferatu to eventually achieve its current reputation as a vampiric classic almost on the same level as Dracula itself.

Center yourself and your thoughts as artist Meera Lee Patel guides you through an exercise to celebrate what makes you you.

Origin: French & Greek, early 19th century

http://track.wordgenius.com/?&eih=lolxmhlsz4q4coz3ctbb1u75szwwyo12&email=jasmind009@gmail.com&partnerCode=&partnerSubcode=

 

1

A dreamlike state in which images both real or imagined blur together

2

A constantly changing series of scenes or events that shift in color and intensity

Welcome to Wellness Week!

We’re serving up some tips (whipped up by you) to help you stay mentally and 
physically healthy. 

 What started out as a forum post 
<https://99designs.community/t/negative-side-effects-of-being-an-artist/327905> 
by@Vesper° talking about the issues that he faced as a creative freelancer, 
turned into an outpouring of advice and support from the community.

 We’ve compiled the highlights for you here to balance out your daily routine 
with juuuuust the right mix, so you can keep on cooking up design magic!

Four steps to staying physically healthy

💧 Step 1: Stay hydrated 
 It can be easy to forget to drink water. And forgetting to drink water can 
lead to a whole host of physical and mental health problems.

✅ Step 2: Set attainable goals 
@VanessaBowman tells us: “We’re all attracted to the idea of big changes, but 
setting unattainable goals sets you up for failure. Set yourself up for success 
with small, attainable goals!”

🤸 Step 3: Start a movement routine
@Bow’n’Pencil says, “Having a daily activity based on your passion or interest 
helps a lot. I spend my daily morning cycling for around an hour.”

🌲 Step 4: Perfect your posture
 Good posture and alleviating pains go hand-in-hand with establishing a 
consistent workout schedule. And when you’re not in pain, you’re more likely to 
work out!
  

Four steps to staying mentally healthy

✂️ Step 1: Cut out negativity
 Sometimes it's hard for people to understand the life of a freelancer. If 
this happens, you can turn to the community in our forum — we’ve heard it 
before, and we’ve got your back!

🐣 Step 2: Find your “why” 
 “You can call it your purpose statement, your personal motivation,’” 
@VanessaBowman recommends revisiting the reasons why you started freelancing in 
the first place to help you move forward.

🚧 Step 3: Set boundaries 
@IsaDesignNet says, “Know when to stop! Not just in theory… but to really 
stop. Stop working at a certain hour every day, which is more difficult than it 
seems when working at home.” 

🔌 Step 4: Find new ways to connect 
 Taking a class or joining a meetup can also be hugely beneficial to build a 
schedule, and it also forces you to put on pants and leave the house. 
  

How do you stay mentally and physically healthy?

subject: You're Invited! Carnegie Mellon University Admission Insights
body_text:
Admission Insights Webinar Series 

Dear Jasmin,

Greetings from Carnegie Mellon University! We know that navigating the college admission process comes with all kinds of questions. Fortunately, we've got answers.

In our Admission Insights Webinar series <https://admission.cmu.edu/portal/admission_insights>, you can hear directly from our admission counselors and campus partners, who'll share their expertise on a variety of topics. Sessions will include:

 Choosing a College: What to Know About Building Your College List
 Writing a College Essay: How to Stand Out in 650 Words or Less
 Admission Decisions: How Colleges Determine the Class
 Financial Aid 101: How to Apply and What to Know
 Pre-College: What to Know About Summer Programming for High Schoolers 

Get the details and register here <https://admission.cmu.edu/portal/admission_insights>!

These events are accessible by Zoom or phone, and you're welcome to invite family or friends to join you. If you can't make it to a live session, don't worry - we'll post recordings of each webinar on our website once they've concluded.

Looking for other ways to engage with us? Register for either a remote information session <https://admission.cmu.edu/portal/remote_info_sessions> or a remote admission counseling session <https://admission.cmu.edu/portal/adm_counseling_session_videocon>! If you have any questions, please contact our office via phone <tel:+1 412.268.2082>, email <mailto:admission@andrew.cmu.edu> or chat <https://www.cmu.edu/admission/>. 

We hope you can join us!Best regards,
Office of Admission

subject: Turning up the heat to get President Trump to move aside at the daily COVID-19 briefings in favor of actual experts

subject: 📢  Join our live webinar on Thursday: What is your portfolio really signaling?
body_text:
Hey Jasmin Duong,

Your portfolio is the most important product you'll ever design
and it is often the first impression your work makes.

Join us on Thursday as Joseph Louis Tan, founder of Career
Creators, breaks down the six questions hiring managers ask when
they first open a portfolio, what those questions are actually
testing for, and how the bar changes from junior to senior.

Save your spot ( https://t.dripemail2.com/c/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..KQZ6oDD3fjUWqpdY0OJTIc5nhXLoefScHZpROdvZ_GY )

Image

-------------------------------
In this session, we’ll explore:
-------------------------------

* what’s happening in today’s UX job market
* the six questions hiring managers ask when they first review
your portfolio
* why strong visuals alone aren’t enough to make your portfolio
stand out
* how portfolio expectations shift from junior to senior level

--------------------------------------------
Is your portfolio sending the right signals?
--------------------------------------------

Selected portfolios will be reviewed in real time using Joseph’s
diagnostic framework, highlighting the signals they send, where
the gaps are, and how they read from junior to senior level.

Submit your portfolio ( https://t.dripemail2.com/c/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..IKNQIg6UHt6poxPG4dlQQLwY2vMcDWpAgCguSsk5eZk )

🎙️ About the Speaker

Joseph Louis Tan is a career coach for experienced designers and
the founder of Career Creators. He has 18 years in design across
six career pivots, from industrial design and lecturing to
fintech, app design, and Head of Product Design at ContactOut. He
is based in Singapore, holds the LinkedIn Top Voice badge since
2024, and has 39,000 followers on LinkedIn.

🗓️ Date: April 2, 2026

🕒 Time: 10:00 AM CEST | 4:00 PM SGT | 1:30 PM IST

Best,

UXfolio team 🖤

---------------------

subject: When the brief lets your imagination soar 🛸
body_text:
A street art project turning vacant storefronts into businesses of the future 

 <http://99designs.com> View in browser 
<http://links.email.99designs.com/e/evib?_t=8276c191798a469d88dfae0dd605a3f8&_m=5fe69aeaf0564293b9b2e4bfb48fde6a&_e=4QNhHz8d2gpBC8sV8yNjdLrXqG_0mm9Ve5SdGk7BxZmJgH8VhrAKKtpT09XmdqCkQkXEjI5CO2V1fmDlrBxPSzqV7rZm6z11yrVHvXMpyQzTpiZjvkq8oyONGCZypcwe>
   
 
<https://www.huckmag.com/art-and-culture/art-2/street-art-project-by-design-tco-london/>

In collaboration with Huck Magazine, we asked five creators from our community 
to design storefronts for imaginary businesses in the empty lots of Britain’s 
high streets. The only necessity was that they look to the future and let 
imagination lead the way!

 
<https://www.huckmag.com/art-and-culture/art-2/street-art-project-by-design-tco-london/>

Fix Your Kicks by Agi Amri

Agnese Sirmā (Agi Amri <https://99designs.com.au/profiles/796402>) is a 
Latvia-based designer known for her intricate illustrations and ink work. Her 
imagined business is Fix Your Kicks, a modern chic cobbler in Manchester 
exclusively repairing and caring for sneakers.

“I loved the idea of designing for an imaginary business. The freedom to draw 
anything I wanted was truly refreshing!”

— Agnese Sirmā (Agi Amri) —

 
<https://www.huckmag.com/art-and-culture/art-2/street-art-project-by-design-tco-london/>
MeMe by Kuziola

Andrzej Kuziola (kuziola <https://99designs.com/profiles/1572543>) is a 
self-taught graphic designer based in Edinburgh. Known for his gothic 
illustrations and fine art. His fantasy storefront is MeMe, a gallery 
showcasing the digital-only art of non-fungible tokens (NFTs) in Glasgow. 

“I had the idea of depicting a mythological goddess or fairy wearing a VR 
headset—then Sandro Botticelli’s 'Birth of Venus' painting came to mind…”

— Andrzej Kuziola (kuziola) — 
 
<https://www.huckmag.com/art-and-culture/art-2/street-art-project-by-design-tco-london/>

Red Location by Radovan Ciobanenco

Another self-taught designer, Radovan Ciobanenco 
<https://99designs.com/profiles/2755727>’s style is a mix of clean minimalism 
blended with subtle bursts of color. His fictional business is Red Location, in 
Kensington, which looks like a regular real estate agency, but a second glance 
reveals the sci-fi twist: the location is Mars!

“I saw this as a challenge that would force me to create outside my comfort 
zone. A lot of my inspiration actually came from a trip to the Canary Islands, 
which is very similar to Mars.”

— Radovan Ciobanenco —

 
<https://www.huckmag.com/art-and-culture/art-2/street-art-project-by-design-tco-london/>

The Broom and the Pebble by Anastasia S.

Ukrainian-based designer Anastasia S. <https://99designs.com/profiles/2639224> 
has an enviable talent for playful character illustrations. Her business is The 
Broom and Pebble, a sports bar celebrating lesser-known (and followed) sports 
such as synchronized swimming, speed climbing, curling, and more!

“It would be amazing if this project inspired interest to visit these areas 
again. I wish we had something like this in my city!”

— Anastasia S. —

 
<https://www.huckmag.com/art-and-culture/art-2/street-art-project-by-design-tco-london/>

Black AI Cafe by GOOSEBUMPS

Dusan Mladenovic (GOOSEBUMPS <https://99designs.com/profiles/1473322>) is a 
self-taught designer from Serbia, specializing in vintage typography and line 
work. His futuristic creation is the Black AI Cafe, in Shoreditch, where the 
baristas are chatty and never forget a name—except they’re not exactly human, 
they’re AI robots!

“My usual style is a mix of vintage and modern inspiration—with this project I 
took it a step further and brought in a futuristic interpretation.”

— Dusan Mladenovic (GOOSEBUMPS) —

Read more about the street art project on Huck Mag

5 Places You Should Live if You Love to Travel
http://tracker.thediscoverer.com/tc?&i=9&t=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thediscoverer.com%2Fcontents%2F5ca6219c62e1d00004d385b9%2Fclick%3Femail%3Djasmind009%40gmail.com%26partnerCode%3D%26partnerSubcode%3D%26mailCampaignSource%3DTheDiscoverer%26mailCampaignId%3D1108824526%26mailMessageId%3D7650771%26mailSegmentId%3D1012088640%26position%3D1%26autosubscribe%3D%26utm_source%3D%26utm_medium%3D%26utm_campaign%3D1108824526%26utm_content%3D7650771%26utm_term%3D1012088640

I’ve roamed the length and breadth of the globe for work and pleasure, but after racking up well over a hundred countries, I can honestly say there’s no place like home. That said, it would be pretty hard being a travel writer if home wasn’t within striking distance of several international airports, well served by public transport and close to a couple of major motorways. If, like me, your life revolves around your next trip, here are five places to live if you love to travel.

Take one of these most scenic train trips in the U.S. for a journey unlike any other.

Art and music are both such beautiful creative expressions. So, when we 
had the opportunity to collaborate with Song Exploder, we couldn’t say YES fast 
enough!

 Host Hrishikesh Hirway handpicked three designers from our global community 
to create a tour poster inspired by the show.

 We took a page out of Hrishi's book and asked our designers to 
'explode' their designs and tell us about what happens when creative 
expressions collide 💥 💥 💥
  

 <https://99designs.com/blog/community/song-exploder-x-99designs-posters/> 

“The first keyword that I transformed into an illustrative element was this 
‘DNA plant’ concept that I’ve had in my head for a while. ‘Vinyl record’ was 
the next one, because everyone loves the warm sound of your favorite vinyl!”

– Eliza Osmo

 <https://99designs.com/blog/community/song-exploder-x-99designs-posters/> 

“I just imagined the ‘exploder’ and thought of something that can explode far 
into space.” 

– Skilline

 <https://99designs.com/blog/community/song-exploder-x-99designs-posters/> 

“The brief didn’t ask for flowers in a vase or people having lunch together, 
it went deeper and I needed to sweat my brain in order to figure out the best 
concept.” 

– Jen Se

subject: How Much Do You Know About World War II?
body_text: Which leader famously said, “We shall fight on the beaches...”?                                                                                                                         Home |   June 29, 2021 How Much Do You Know About World War II? Picture Alliance/ Contributor/ Getty Images Pelé's First World Cup June 29, 1958 Today, Brazil is known for dominating the World Cup, having won five titles since the tournament began in 1930 — more than any other nation. But in the first half of the 20th century, the South American country had often disappointed in international competition. That all changed on June 29, 1958, when a young Edson Arantes do Nascimento — better known as Pelé — led the Brazilian team to their very first World Cup title. Seventeen-year-old Pelé’s legend-defining moment came in the semi-finals of the tournament, when he scored three times — known as a hat-trick — against France. In the finals, the teen shocked the home crowd in Stockholm, leading Brazil to defeat Sweden for the World Cup. Pelé went on to lead Brazil to another two titles (in 1962 and 1970), and to this day he has the most World Cup wins of any player in history. One of the greatest soccer players in the history of the game, Pelé is lovingly known in Brazil as "O Rei" — "The King." Ffern is redefining what brand storytelling can look like. By treating each seasonal release as a cinematic experience, the fragrance label moves beyond traditional campaigns into immersive world-building. Between their in-house film team and commitment to real environments, Ffern is crafting something slower, richer, and far more emotionally resonant.

Beyond the campaign: Exploring Ffern’s cinematic brand world

At the core of Ffern’s success is its commitment to storytelling through film. Rather than relying on fast-paced campaigns, the perfumery produces seasonal cinematic shorts that mirror the craft and emotion of its fragrances. Shot in real landscapes and conditions, each film captures fleeting moments in nature while inviting audiences into immersive, sensory worlds where they can almost experience the scents.

This approach is deeply rooted in the founders’ upbringing and their shared love of filmmaking. By showing both the final films and the process behind them, Ffern is growing by building trust and authenticity in an industry often dominated by polish and celebrity endorsement. The result is a brand system where narrative, craft, and experience are inseparable.

Blending heritage, sound, and street culture with the new Sprite

Sprite’s latest rebrand proves that evolution doesn’t always mean reinvention. By reintroducing its iconic Lymon symbol and refining core design elements, the brand leans into nostalgia while modernizing for today’s multi-platform world. Paired with a new sonic identity and deeper ties to music and street culture, Sprite’s update reaches beyond a visual refresh and into a full sensory experience. While many consumers are looking to nostalgia for comfort, Sprite’s revival is a strategic update balancing recognizability, cultural relevance, and global scalability.

body_text: Email from Community Servings Cookies Everyone will Accept.....and Enjoy!   A Sweet Way to Celebrate Valentine's Day When you Spread the Love this Valentine’s Day, your gift does more than spoil someone special—it helps nourish a neighbor facing critical illness. With a $35 donation to support our meals program, your recipient will receive a beautifully designed Valentine’s Day card featuring your personal message, while a client at Community Servings receives a full week of scratch-made, medically tailored meals prepared in our Boston-based kitchen and delivered to their home. For gifts of $65 or $95, your Valentine will also receive a handcrafted box of freshly baked Top Shelf Cookies, featuring limited-edition flavors created just for the season. The Valentine's Card ($35) Your recipient will receive a personalized greeting card, providing a week of nutritious, scratch-made, medically tailored meals. Double The Love Gift Box ($65) Your recipient will receive a custom card plus six gourmet cookies: Red Line - a red velvet cookie with white chocolate chips, and Back Bay Berry Bliss - a raspberry cookie with chocolate chips. This gift supports two weeks of medically tailored meals for a neighbor experiencing illness. The Valentine's Day Sampler ($95) Includes our custom Valentine's Day card and a variety of individually wrapped cookies, including Red Line - Red Velvet, Hazel's Chocolate Chip, XOXO - Ruby Chocolate Sprinkles, and Back Bay Berry Bliss. This gift supports three weeks of medically tailored meals for a neighbor experiencing illness. SEND A VALENTINE'S GIFT! Thank You to our Spread the Love Sponsor! Shopping cart will close on February 8 at 5pm. subject: You can’t build great AI without great data: RAG with MongoDB and Python
body_text:
To view this email as a web page, go to the following address: https://info.mongodb.com/index.php/email/emailWebview?mkt_tok=MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgfGwhGYUnKTNGc_rDBtm3psZjcEzFyGCXjbkWSMLug4C0wlQa6NdAmMjzeH8ctCigpoa5-68zoQ6v7xuessRs79hyuWuqgzC-9rewTb3O1f8z-w 

Hi Jasmin,


Large language models are only as smart as the data you feed them. That’s why retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is such a critical skill to master.

Join us on March 18 at 11am ET for our fourth session in the MongoDB & Python Development Series, MongoDB for Python Builders: RAG <https://em.mongodb.com/MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgfGwhGZNwIqaneRyfmu_fdn6OyopoM4u_jWlsRIzkj7nO5jHUF-B17f3nHjt1NvUaUpkaz64=>. We’ll show you how to architect production-ready RAG applications. Uplevel your AI development and learn the following skills:


	- Architecting RAG workflows that ground your LLMs in real-time, proprietary data
	- Optimizing the retrieval process for low-latency, accurate results
	- Managing both vector and original source data within a single, unified data platform



MongoDB experts will be available for 1:1 support to help you troubleshoot issues and answer your questions in live time as we go through hands-on challenges. 

Additionally, you’ll have another opportunity to earn a MongoDB Skill Badge during the workshop that you can add to your LinkedIn profile to showcase your expertise in modern data architecture. 

If you want to catch up on Part 3: MongoDB and Vector Search in 
Python <https://em.mongodb.com/MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgfGwhGSVpGM8BEFq8dZCjj4MZrNkuFmFWyoQ3CUlfstQd8nMzJ2t-7W1fW1d9Or7E_mnJAVE=>, the recording is now on-demand. You can also still complete the corresponding Skill 
Badge <https://em.mongodb.com/MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgfGwhGaXhlgpcLAp4KJEgFMuW0RjYCx7unxZkNHA3vXDL0inB3FLxHRNOd6vPxuRPrBgX0yQ=>.

Ready to start building intelligent software that reasons with your data?
Register now <https://em.mongodb.com/MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgfGwhGZNwIqaneRyfmu_fdn6OyopoM4u_jWlsRIzkj7nO5jHUF-B17f3nHjt1NvUaUpkaz64=>
Think Big, Go Far,
The MongoDB Team

Figma's public offering: A game-changer for design founders, investors, and the tech market

Figma’s recent IPO was a resounding success, showing us just how integral design tools are to the tech ecosystem while bringing both financial validation and strategic growth to the design industry. While the IPO raised $1.2 billion, the real story is in the structure, focused on liquidity for investors while ensuring founder control. This move could inspire other design tool companies to go public, signaling a shift where AI, long-term growth, and high control are key to success.

As the IPO market rebounds, this is a clear indicator for design founders and investors: it’s time to think strategically about scaling and liquidity. Figma’s public offering marks a game-changing moment for design in tech and a bright horizon for future startups looking to attract investment while controlling their narratives.

Transforming a town with street art: The power of Weston Wallz festival

Weston-super-Mare has transformed from a sleepy seaside town into a lively open-air gallery thanks to the Weston Wallz annual 9-day street art festival. With international artists contributing vibrant murals across the town, the festival has sparked a cultural and economic revival. The festival has not only improved the town’s aesthetics but also creates community engagement, making art accessible for all. Beyond aesthetics, Weston Wallz has boosted tourism, raised property values, and created a sense of unity.
